Consent Calendar Item Overview: 6a: Approval of Minutes –Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees: September 15, 2026 6b: Approve Supervisor to Sign Renewal with Decker Insurance – Dexter Township has utilized Decker Insurance Agency for many years as the provider of our comprehensive Public Entity Insurance Package, which includes property and liability coverage. The renewal proposal for the upcoming policy period, effective November 1, 2026, through October 31, 2027, reflects a total premium of $34,320. This represents an 8.5% increase over the current year’s premium, which is considerably lower than the 13.9% increase experienced in 2025. The 8.5% increase is consistent with what was anticipated based on previous conversations with Decker Insurance representatives. The Township has also benefited from $2,807 in dividends and grants awarded through the program in recent years. 6c: Approval of Board and Committee Appointments – There are currently two appointments to consider for the Dexter Library Board. One current board member is seeking reappointment, with a new term beginning October 1, 2026, and ending September 30, 2030. The second appointment is for a new board member, with a term beginning October 1, 2026, and ending September 30, 2030. The second member considering appointment is a 15-year resident of Dexter with an educational background is in chemistry. They retired in 2025 after a career as a corporate scientist and technology executive across multiple industrial businesses (see resume). They currently sit on one corporate board (Lincoln Electric Co.), and prior to moving to Michigan, they served for 2 years on a public library board for the 9 branches of the Schenectady Country Public Library, in Schenectady, NY. These terms expire in September and run for 4 years in accordance with the Dexter Library’s establishment agreement. We are always grateful to the individuals who generously volunteer their time to serve on our boards, committees, and commissions, and we would especially like to thank Jim LaVoie for more than 30 years of dedicated service on the Dexter Library Board. His longstanding commitment and service to the Library and the Dexter community are greatly appreciated. Finally, additional terms and appointments will be considered by the Township Board at its December meeting. 6d: Approval for Appraisal for Property 2026-6 per the FOSP Board - At its October 1, 2026 meeting, the Farmland and Open Space Preservation Board recommend an appraisal for Property 2026-6 for $3,200. Submitted by: Supervisor Scott Suggested language: Motion to approve the consent agenda for October 20, 2026. 3 of 226 Dexter Township 6880 Dexter-Pinckney Road Dexter, MI 48130 Telephone: 734-426-3767 Fax: 734-426-3833 www.dextertownshipmi.gov Lonnie Scott Supervisor Michelle Stamboulellis Clerk Bradley Metz Treasurer Alicia Abbott Karen Nolte Laura Sanders Karen Sikkenga Trustees Dexter Township Board – Regular Meeting Tuesday September 15, 2026 – 6:00PM Location: Dexter Township Hall, 6880 Dexter-Pinckney Rd., Dexter, MI Call to Order: Supervisor Scott called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM. Acknowledgements: Optional Pledge of Allegiance Roll Call/Conflict of Interest Check Present: Trustee Nolte, Trustee Abbott, Treasurer Metz, Clerk Stamboulellis, Trustee Sanders, Trustee Sikkenga, Supervisor Scott. Absent – None All members declared no conflict of interest. Approval of Agenda Prior to the first call for public comment, the agenda was amended Supervisor Scott noted the following amendments prior to the motion: the Metro Act Resolution was moved from the consent agenda to Action Item E; a resolution of support for the Michigan Township Participating Plan grant application was added as Action Item F; and the approval of minutes was removed from the consent agenda and added as Action Item A. The board accepted amendments as part of a single motion. Motion to approve the agenda as amended. Moved by Trustee Abbott, seconded by Treasurer Metz. All Ayes. Motion carried. Call for Public Comment Joseph Spiegel addressed the board regarding a University of Michigan town hall meeting about a data center project in Ypsilanti Township, expressing concern about the lack of community engagement, NDAs signed by participants, and the university's exemption from local zoning ordinances. He distributed a draft resolution for board consideration that would prohibit NDAs in matters involving Dexter Township and encouraged the board to review two pending house bills that would address public university zoning exemptions. Consent Agenda: Motion to approve the consent agenda as amended. Moved by Trustee Nolte, seconded by Treasurer Metz. All Ayes. Motion carried. Minutes of the Dexter Township Board September 15, 2026 Closed Session – Attorney Consultation pursuant to MCL 15.268 (1)(h) Motion to enter closed session pursuant to MCL 15.268(1)(h) for attorney consultation was made by Trustee Sikkenga and seconded by Treasurer Metz. The motion carried by unanimous roll call vote. The board returned to open session thereafter. Motion to exit closed session. Moved by Treasurer Metz, seconded by Trustee Sikkenga. All Ayes. Motion carried. Action Items a) Acceptance of Financial Transactions Trustee Sikkenga raised several housekeeping notes, including ensuring election-related postage and contracted services are captured for reimbursement which Clerk Stamboulellis confirmed that she was in the process of submitting those reimbursements, and that budgeted transfers to the capital fund be executed, and a question regarding the coding of a Carlisle Wortman expense to engineering rather than planning. Motion to accept the financial transactions. Moved by Trustee Sikkenga, seconded by Treasurer Metz. All Ayes. Motion carried. b) Approval of Resolution #26-714 Dementia Friendly Initiatives Motion to approve Resolution #26-714 Moved by Clerk Stamboulellis, seconded by Treasurer Metz. All Ayes. Motion carried. c) Bed and Breakfast Ordinance Amendment Trustee Sanders introduced the resolution, noting she had spent the prior month in preparation, consulting with County Clerk Kestenbaum, Youssef Robbie, Sheriff Alex Thomas, and Maria Barrafrey of We the People regarding how townships and clerks should respond should ICE agents appear at polling locations. She described a growing collaborative effort at both the county and state level to develop best practices and training resources for clerks and indicated her intent to work internally with the Board and Clerk to develop a preparedness plan. Motion to approve the Bed and Breakfast Ordinance Amendment with the events subsection (Section 6) removed. Moved by Trustee Sikkenga, seconded by Treasurer Sanders. Motion made by roll call vote: Trustee Nolte – No; Trustee Abbott – Yes; Treasurer Metz – No; Clerk Stamboulellis – No; Trustee Sanders – Yes; Trustee Sikkenga – Yes; Supervisor Scott – Yes. Motion carried 4-3, with Trustee Nolte, Clerk Stamboulellis and Treasurer Metz voting no. d. FY 2027 Capital Budget Amendment: Roof Replacement Supervisor Scott noted the roof replacement is being advanced ahead of the original capital plan schedule in anticipation of a potential solar installation, and that the roof is approximately 25 Page 2 of 5 Minutes of the Dexter Township Board September 15, 2026 years old. The amendment was noted to be for transparency purposes, as the overall capital fund budget was already approved at the fund level. Motion to approve the FY 2027 Capital Budget Amendment for roof replacement. Moved by Trustee Sikkenga, seconded by Trustee Abbott. Motion made by roll call vote: Trustee Nolte – Yes; Trustee Abbott – Yes; Treasurer Metz – Yes; Clerk Stamboulellis – Yes; Trustee Sanders – Yes; Trustee Sikkenga – Yes; Supervisor Scott – Yes. Motion carried. e. METRO Act Resolution #26-713 Township Attorney provided background on the Metro Act, explaining it is among the least favorable telecom statutes for local units of government, with compensation capped at 5 cents per square foot and a penalty of up to $40,000 per day for non-compliance past the 45-day approval deadline. The application from SURF Internet was described as complete and well-prepared. SURF's proposed installation involves fiber optic cable for broadband and telecom service in the Portage Lake area of the township, using existing infrastructure. Clerk Stamboulellis noted questions about whether SURF had obtained a right-ofway permit from the Washtenaw County Road Commission, which the attorney confirmed is a condition of the township's approval. Motion to adopt Resolution #26-713 Moved by Trustee Sikkenga and seconded by Treasurer Metz. Motion made by roll call vote: Trustee Nolte – Yes; Trustee Abbott – Yes; Treasurer Metz – Yes; Clerk Stamboulellis – Yes; Trustee Sanders – Yes; Trustee Sikkenga – Yes; Supervisor Scott – Yes. The resolution was adopted 7-0. f. Authorize Dexter Township to Submit Fire Equipment Grant Application on Behalf of the Dexter Area Fire Department and Execute Any Required Grant Documents Supervisor Scott explained this supplemental item is a resolution of support for a Michigan Township Participating Plan grant of up to $2,500 for security cameras at Fire Station 2, to be installed at exterior locations, within bays, and facing interior doors. The grant mirrors an existing camera system at Station 1. Supervisor Scott confirmed that footage is not stored, is accessible only by the fire chief and one officer and is reviewed solely in the event of an incident. Motion to approve Resolution #26-715 in support for the Michigan Township Participating Grant. Moved by Trustee Sikkenga and seconded by Clerk Stamboulellis. Motion made by roll call vote: Trustee Nolte – Yes; Trustee Abbott – Yes; Treasurer Metz – Yes; Clerk Stamboulellis – Yes; Trustee Sanders – Yes; Trustee Sikkenga – Yes; Supervisor Scott – Yes. The resolution was adopted 7-0. Discussion Items: Motion to move discussion f (Millelson Conditional Rezoning) to letter A. Moved by Trustee Nolte, seconded by Treasurer Metz. All Ayes. Motion carried. a) Mikkelson Conditional Rezoning Request Sustainability Partnership Resolution Page 3 of 5 Minutes of the Dexter Township Board September 15, 2026 Director Reyher summarized the conditional rezoning request from the Mikkelson’s, who are seeking to rezone their property from Recreation Conservation to Rural Residential in order to split the parcel for residential use following the cessation of campground operations. The rezoning is consistent with surrounding properties, and voluntary conditions offered by the applicants limit use to single-family residential. No public opposition was received. The board expressed no concerns, and Supervisor Scott indicated the item will be placed on the consent agenda for the October meeting. b) Roofing Bids Three bids were received in response to an RFP for reroofing the township building. One vendor submitted bids for both metal ($138,000) and shingle ($35,000) options; two other vendors submitted shingle-only bids. A decision is expected at the next meeting. c) Additional STR Ban Enforcement Trustee Nolte reported visiting an open house at a property she suspected was operating as a short-term rental (STR), where the owner openly acknowledged its current STR use. She subsequently filed a complaint with the township and noted that she and Director Reyher had been tracking two separate properties. The board discussed the challenge of enforcement, including the difficulty of pursuing anonymous complaints, and the limitations of the current civil penalty structure, which begins at $500 per violation under state statute. Director Reyher noted that two STR listings have since been removed from VRBO. The board discussed whether to pursue known active listings proactively, with Supervisor Scott clarifying that STRs were always a non-permitted use under existing zoning, and that the township's enforcement path is through that mechanism. The discussion concluded with support from Clerk Stamboulellis for including a part-time code enforcement officer in the upcoming FY 2028 budget proposal. d. Snow Removal Supervisor Scott noted that a snow removal vendor was not selected during the lawn care RFP process and that a selection will be made at the October meeting. e. FY 2028 Budget Requests Supervisor Scott reminded board members that budget season is underway and requested that all project requests and budget items be submitted for consolidation. Staff have already begun building the budget spreadsheet for FY 2028. f. Sustainability Partnership Resolution Trustee Sikkenga described an opportunity to partner with the University of Michigan Graham Institute for Sustainability, through which a class of six graduate students would assess the township's environmental sustainability practices using a rubric developed in partnership with Michigan Communities. Students would earn academic credit for the assessment, and a subsequent class would carry out selected action items. Trustee Sikkenga noted that a formal resolution of support will be brought to the board for approval at the next meeting. Q&A: Staff and Dexter Township Committee Reports a. Office Administrator Report – Samatha Edwards b. Supervisor Report – Supervisor Scott Supervisor Scott reported that a vendor for the exterior tree clearing has been approved for a cost of $900, following receipt of two additional bids after the original quote exceeded $3,000. c. Clerk Report – Clerk Stamboulellis Page 4 of 5 Minutes of the Dexter Township Board September 15, 2026 Clerk Stamboulellis noted that the Dexter township Elections Coffee Chat is scheduled for October 24th and that ballot will be mailed out on September 21st. d. Treasurer Report – Treasurer Metz e. Planning Commission and Zoning Board of Appeals – Fletcher Reyher Director Reyher provided an updated DPZ report, distributed as supplemental material. f. FOSP Board – Clerk Stamboulellis g. Farmland @ Open Space Preservation Board – Barry Lonik h. Huron River Watershed Council – Sue Bade, Dexter Township i. Trustee Report — Trustee Abbott & Trustee Sanders j. Trustee Report – Trustee Abbott l. WWRA Report – Clerk Stamboulellis Trustee Sikkenga noted the first meeting of the local roads policy subcommittee was held that day, and that reports on the subcommittee's work will begin at the next meeting. Trustee Sikkenga also recognized the fire chief and department for their response during the recent storm. Data & Performance Metrics a. Fire Department Activities b. Sheriff's Department Activities Fire and Sheriff’s Department activity reports were received and distributed as supplemental material. Second Call for Public Comment None Other Issues, Comments and Concerns of Board Members & Staff Trustee Nolte reminded volunteers to contact the office regarding the upcoming cleanup day on September 17th, including availability. Treasurer Metz thanked residents for their patience on the final tax payment day, noting the office was exceptionally busy throughout the day, Supervisor Scott also thanked all office staff for their work during the tax deadline period. Supervisor Scott also thanked Nick Stamboulellis for cutting up and hauling away the tree limbs that fell in the Hudson Mills Cemetery. Adjournment: There being no further business, Supervisor Scott adjourned the meeting at 8:21pm. (b) To manage and supervise all public improvements, works, and undertakings of the township; (c) To have charge of the construction, repair, maintenance, lighting and cleaning of streets, sidewalks, bridges, pavements, sewers, and of all the public buildings or other property belonging to the township; (d) To manage and supervise the operation of all township utilities; (e) To be responsible for the preservation of property, tools, and appliances of the township; (f) To see that all terms and conditions imposed in favor of the township or its inhabitants in any public utility franchise, or in any contract, are faithfully kept and performed; (g) To attend all meetings of the township board, with the right to take part in discussions, but without the right to vote; (h) To be a member, ex officio, of all committees of the township board; (i) To prepare and administer the annual budget under policies formulated by the township board and keep the said board fully advised at all times as to the financial condition and needs of the township; (j) To recommend to the township board for adoption such measures as he may deem necessary or expedient; (k) To be responsible to the township board for the efficient administration of all departments of the township government; (l) To act as the purchasing agent for the township or, under his responsibility, delegate such duties to some other officer or employee; (m) To conduct all sales of personal property which the township board may authorize to be sold; (n) To assume all the duties and responsibilities as personnel director of all township employees or delegate such duties to some other officer or employee; (o) To perform such other duties as may be prescribed by this act or required of him by ordinance or by direction of the township board, or which are not assigned to some other official in conformity with the provisions of this act. Charter township boards generally are considerably less involved in administrative matters than general law township boards, as the Charter Township Act expressly assigns responsibility for day to day administration to the supervisor or superintendent. PRESENT: TRUSTEE — Sheila Bussell SUPERVISOR — Al VanWashenova TRUSTEE — Chris Collins - EXCUSED CLERK — Kyle Bryant TRUSTEE — Kraig Yoas TREASURER — Julie Ellison TRUSTEE — Gary Klemz TWP ATTORNEY — Kerry Bondy DEPUTY CLERK - Jessica Burt Township Public Safety/Economic Development Director, Dave Uhl; Fire Chief, Wendy Stevens; Building Official, Gary Dahl; Cert Director, Mark Donaldson; Makers Market Director, Jon Ramsey and 15 persons were in attendance. Supervisor VanWashenova called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM. CHANGES TO THE AGENDA: None MOTION #26.287 — AGENDA APPROVAL: Motion made by Mr. Yoas; seconded by Mrs. Bussell to approve the September 22, 2026 agenda as presented. A voice vote was taken. Motion carried 6-0. MOTION #26.288 — APPROVAL OF SEPTEMBER 22, 2026 CONSENT AGENDA: Motion made by Mrs. Ellison; seconded by Mr. Yoas to approve the consent agenda as presented. A roll call vote was taken. Mr. Klemz- Yes; Mrs. Ellison-Yes; Mr. VanWashenova-Yes; Mr. Bryant-Yes; Mrs. Bussell-Yes; Mr. Yoas-Yes. Motion carried 6-0. CONSENT AGENDA: a. September 15, 2026 — Regular Board Meeting Minutes b. Invoices paid between September 16, 2026 to September 18, 2026 c. Invoices Paid on September 22, 2026 PUBLIC COMMENT: Maria Zagorski introduced herself to the Board and stated she is running for Circuit judge. One person stated that the Board shouldn’t have removed Flock cameras. Three persons spoke of Flock concerns, light at the Detroit beach subdivision and the Township’s Halloween event. One person spoke that the Township lacks transparency and communication. MOTION #26.289 - DISCUSSION — 28? READING OF ZONING ORDINANCE AMENDMENT NO. 300- 20 — OFF — STREET PARKING DEVELOPMENT: Motion made by Mr. Klemz; seconded by Mr. Bryant to approve the 2" reading and adoption of Zoning Ordinance Amendment 300-20. A roll call vote was taken. Mr. VanWashenova- Yes; Mr. Bryant-Yes; Mrs. Ellison-Yes; Mr. Klemz-Yes; Mr. Yoas-No; Mrs. Bussell-Yes. Motion September 22, 2026 — Regular Township Meeting Minutes — Page 2: carried 5-1. MOTION #26.290 — DISCUSSION — 2027 MAKERS MARKET FEES: Motion made by Mr. Bryant; seconded by Mr. Klemz to approve the 2027 Makers Market fee schedule as presented. A roll call vote was taken. Mr. Klemz-Yes; Mr. Yoas-Yes; Mrs. Ellison-Yes; Mrs. Bussell- Yes; Mr. Van Washenova-Yes; Mr. Bryant-Yes. Motion carried 6-0. DISCUSSION — FRENCHTOWN CERT DIRECTOR PRESENTATION: Cert Director Donaldson gave a presentation to the Board. MOTION #26.291— DISCUSSION — PURCHASE REQUEST IPADS — FRENCHTOWN FIRE DEPARTMENT: Motion made by Mrs. Ellison; seconded by Mr. Klemz to approve the Fire Chief to purchase 9 iPads with accessories at a presented at a cost not to exceed $11,099.55. A roll call vote was taken. Mr. Klemz- Yes; Mr. Yoas-Yes; Mrs. Bussell-Yes; Mrs. Ellison-Yes; Mr. VanWashenova-Yes; Mr. Bryant-Yes. Motion carried 6-0. MOTION #26,.292 — DISCUSSION — AUTHORIZE BOARD MEMBER TO EXECUTE CLOSING DOCUMENTS: Motion made by Mr. Bryant; seconded by Mrs. Bussell to authorize the Township Clerk to execute the closing documents for the two closings with Aldrich on the North Dixie Highway 5 acre more or less sale and 10 acre more or less purchase. A roll call vote was taken. Mr. Klemz-Yes; Mrs. Bussell-Yes; Mrs. Ellison-Yes; Mr. Yoas-Yes; Mr. Bryant-Yes; Mr. VanWashenova- Yes. Motion carried 6-0. MOTION #26.293— DISCUSSION — CORRIDOR IMPROVEMENT AUTHORITY BOARD APPOINTMENTS: Motion made by Mr. Klemz; seconded by Mrs. Ellison to approve the re-appointments of Nick Tsipis and Joel Pym with terms to expire July 15, 2030 and to appoint John Cascardo as a new member to fill the vacancy of Dustin Schultze for the remainder of his term as presented. A roll call vote was taken. Mr. Yoas- Yes; Mrs. Bussell-Yes; Mr. Klemz-Yes; Mrs. Ellison-Yes; Mr. VanWashenova-Yes; Mr. Bryant-Yes. Motion carried 6-0. MOTION #26.294 -DISCUSSION —DEMO BIDS — 3419 FERNWOOD: Motion made by Mr. Yoas; seconded by Mrs. Ellison to approve the demolition bid for David Hoffman for 3419 Fernwood contingent upon the Judge approving the demolition order. A roll call vote was taken. Mr. Klemz-Yes; Mr. VanWashenova-Yes; Mrs. Ellison-Yes; Mr. Bryant-Yes; Mrs. Bussell-Yes; Mr. Yoas-Yes. Motion carried 6-0. MOTION #26.295 — DISCUSSION —2027 TAX ROLL RESOLUTIONS: Motion made by Mrs. Ellison; seconded by Mr. Yoas to approve the 2027 Tax Roll Resolutions for the Township Operating, Resort District and Fire Department Fund Resolutions as presented. A roll call vote was taken. Mr. VanWashenova-Yes; Mr. Klemz- Yes; Mrs. Ellison-Yes; Mr. Bryant-Yes; Mrs. Bussell-Yes; Mr. Yoas-Yes. Motion carried 6-0. MOTION #26.296 — DISCUSSION —2027 LAKE ERIE TRANSIT TAX ROLL RESOLUTION: Motion made by Mr. Bryant; seconded by Mrs. Bussell to approve the 2027 Lake Erie Transit Resolution. A roll call vote was taken. Mr. Yoas-No; Mr. Klemz-Yes; Mrs. Ellison-Yes; Mrs. Bussell-Yes; Mr. Bryant-Yes; Mr. Van Washenova- Yes. Motion carried 5-1. text: FRENCHTOWN CHARTER TOWNSHIP RESOLUTION TO APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS THE USE WITH SPECIFIC STANDARDS APPLICATION SUBMITTED BY DTE ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR THE FERMI ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM Adopted October ___, 2026 WHEREAS, on August 14, 2026, Frenchtown Charter Township (Township) received an application for a Use with Specific Standards Approval (SUP) and Site Plan Approval from DTE Electric Company (DTE) consisting of (1) an application form, (2) an application narrative, (3) a site plan, including a preliminary haul route plan and landscape plan, (4) a sound study, (5) an environmental impacts analysis and wetland delineation study, (6) an emergency response plan, (7) a waste mitigation plan, (8) a decommissioning plan and form of agreement, (9) a form of indemnity agreement (10) a complaint resolution form, (11) an operations agreement, (12) a drainage plan, (13) a topographic survey, and (14) proof of ownership (collectively the Application); and WHEREAS, the proposed Fermi Energy Battery Energy Storage System (Project) is for a Utility Scale (200 MW x 4 hrs/800 MW over 4 hrs) battery energy storage system (BESS) located in a PS Public Service Zoning District of the Township on Parcel No. 58-07-528-013-00, which is located at Toll Road and Enrico Fermi Drive and being approximately 51.37 acres, which is property of DTE; and WHEREAS, the Township received reports as to the SUP and site plan applications from Township Engineer Mannik Smith Group dated September 10, 2026 which respectively stated that the Engineer had no objection to a recommendation of special use approval and the grant of final site plan approval subject to certain conditions identified in the reports and from Township Planner David Arthur Consultants dated September 22, 2026 which respectively recommended that DTE’s Applications for SUP and site plan approval be approved again with certain conditions identified in the reports; and WHEREAS, on October 13, 2026 DTE submitted a letter to the Township in response to the David Arthur Consultants Reports providing some clarification and generally concurring with the conditions and recommendations of the Planner and Engineer Reports; and WHEREAS, on October 15, 2026, the Township Planning Commission held a duly noticed public hearing to consider the DTE Application and to receive comments from the public, and Applicant DTE, as well as to review the Mannik Smith Group and David Arthur Consultants Reports; and WHEREAS, in reliance upon DTE’s Application, submissions and representations and the Mannik Smith Group and David Arthur Consultants Reports, the Planning Commission by motion recommended to the Township Board approval of the SUP Application subject to certain conditions identified by the Planning Commission and by separate motion approved the final site plan application subject again to certain additional conditions identified by the Planning Commission and including but not limited to the conditions identified in both the Page 1 of 4 Mannik and David Arthur Consultants Reports, and subject to approval of the SUP Application by the Township Board; and NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Township Board subject to compliance with the reasonable conditions stated below, makes the following findings as to the Project and the requirements of the Township Zoning Ordinance as to SUP Requirements for Battery Energy Storage Systems and Section 7.04(A)(2) Uses with Specific Standard Approval as follows: 1. The use is compatible with adjacent zoning, location, design, size, and intensity of use; 2. The use will not adversely impact traffic operations; 3. The use will not have adverse impacts on groundwater or stormwater runoff; 4. The use will not adversely impact demand on public facilities and services; 5. The use proposes a Project that complies with the BESS-specific Ordinance requirements and minimizes potential impacts; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that in reliance upon DTE’s Application and representations as well as the Mannik Smith Group and David Arthur Consultants Reports, the Frenchtown Charter Township Board hereby approves DTE’s SUP Application subject to and conditioned upon certain reasonable conditions which are in keeping with the spirit and intent of the Zoning Ordinance and which will help to protect neighboring properties and the community from a negative impact which are as follows: 1. Prior to construction, DTE shall comply with all applicable local, state, and federal laws and regulations, and provide evidence of all necessary permits demonstrating compliance to the Building Official prior to performing any work requiring that permit. 2. Prior to construction, DTE and the Township shall enter into a mutually agreeable Decommissioning Agreement in form and substance similar to the agreement submitted by DTE with its Application, which provides for a surety bond for the estimated cost of decommissioning. 3. Prior to construction, DTE and the Township shall enter into a mutually agreeable Indemnity Agreement that accurately describes the Project and location. 4. Prior to construction, DTE and the Township shall enter into a Host Community Agreement as required by the Zoning Ordinance requiring that, upon commencement of operations, DTE will pay the Township $2,000 per MW of nameplate capacity to be used as determined by the Township for 2 police, fire, public safety, or other Township infrastructure, or for other agreed upon projects such as roads, public improvement projects or such other uses as set forth in the Agreement. 5. Prior to construction, DTE shall submit a sound modeling study for the onsite backup generators to provide for the attenuation of the generators which is to the satisfaction of the Township Building Official. Within 120 days after commencement of operations, DTE shall also submit a postconstruction noise monitoring report to the Township Building Official demonstrating Ordinance compliance, including during generator testing, and correct any demonstrated exceedance. 6. Prior to construction, if required by the Monroe County Road Commission, DTE shall enter into an agreement with the Monroe County Road Commission and post a financial obligation in an amount agreeable to the Monroe County Road Commission for impacts to county roads, and submit evidence of the agreement and financial obligation to the Building Official. 7. Prior to construction, DTE shall obtain any necessary approvals, from the Monroe County Drain Commissioner, enter into any required agreements with the Drain Commissioner, and post any financial obligation required by the Drain Commissioner for impacts to county drains and the management of stormwater, and shall provide the Township Building Official with evidence of the approvals, agreements, and financial obligation. 8. Prior to construction, DTE shall submit a complete and satisfactory Emergency Response Plan and DTE shall provide evidence confirming the Fire Chief’s approval of the proposed plan to the Township Building Official. 9. Prior to construction, DTE shall comply with all comments and recommendations of the Township Planner and Engineer reports as to SUP and site plan approval and DTE shall provide an updated final site plan and supporting documents to the Building Official that addresses the items and conditions identified in the Mannik Smith Group Report and the David Arthur Consultants Report. The updated materials shall include the following: i. A description of how DTE will address parking for vehicles that access the Project site during operations. ii. Labeling the current land uses of adjoining properties and properties across the street in the site plan. iii. Providing a physical and chemical analysis of the soil. iv. Addressing site lighting and hours of operation of the site lighting. 3 10. Post-construction, DTE shall provide as-built drawings of all the proposed facilities and Project components such as the containers, access roads, fences, inverters, junction boxes, and underground collection system. The as-built drawings required under this section shall be provided within a reasonable time following completion of construction as determined by the Building Official. The foregoing resolution offered by Board Member Second offered by Board Member Upon roll call vote the following voted “aye”: “nay”: Absent/Excused: The Supervisor declared the resolution adopted. AGENDA Call to Order: Pledge of Allegiance: Introductions: Conflict of Interest: Approval of Agenda: Call to the Public: (Please Note: The Board will not begin any new business after 10:00 p.m) OLD BUSINESS: 1. 26-15…A request by Michael Prudhomme, 3592 Kipling Circle, for rear and side yard setback variances and any other variances deemed necessary by the Zoning Board of Appeals, to build a detached garage. NEW BUSINESS: 1. 26-16…A request by Dennis & Patricia Pereira, 3859 Homestead Dr., for waterfront yard setback variance and any other variances deemed necessary by the Zoning Board of Appeals, to demolish an existing home and build a new home. ADMINISTRATIVE BUSINESS: 1. 2. 3. 4. Approval of minutes for the September 15, 2026 Zoning Board of Appeals meeting. Correspondence Member Discussion Adjournment *Citizen’s Comments- In addition to providing the public with an opportunity to address the Township Board at the beginning of the meeting, opportunity to comment on individual agenda items may be offered by the Chairman as they are presented. Anyone speaking on an agenda item will be limited to 2 minutes. *UPDATED* MEMORANDUM TO: FROM: DATE: Genoa Township Zoning Board of Appeals Carrie Aulette, Zoning Official September 29, 2026 RE: ZBA 26-15 STAFF REPORT File Number: ZBA#26-15 Site Address: 3592 Kipling Circle Parcel Number: 4711-19-302-029 Parcel Size: 1.47 Acres Applicant: Michael Prudhomme, Owner Property Owner: Same as applicant Information Submitted: Application, site plan, conceptual drawings Request: Dimensional Variance Project Description: Applicant is requesting a side & rear yard setback variance to construct a new accessory building. Zoning and Existing Use: RPUD (Residential Planned Unit Development) Other: Public hearing was published in the Livingston County Press and Argus on Sunday August 30, 2026 and 300-foot mailings were sent to any real property within 300 feet of the property in accordance with the Michigan Zoning Enabling Act. Background The following is a brief summary of the background information we have on file: • • • • Per Township Records, the home was built in 1998. The parcel is serviced by well & septic. See Assessing Record Card. The sign location has been reviewed by the Utility Director Summary: The applicant is requesting a side & rear yard setback to construct a new accessory building. Per the PUD agreement for Novel Estates, all structures must comply with the same setbacks as the principal buildings. Summary of Findings of Fact- After reviewing the application and materials provided, I offer the possible findings of fact for your consideration: Please note that in order for a variance to be approved it has to meet all of the standards in 23.05.03. (a) Practical Difficulty/Substantial Justice – Strict compliance with the required setback would create a practical difficulty by significantly limiting the reasonable placement of the proposed detached accessory building. The rear corner provides the most practical location without requiring extensive excavation or placing the building in the center of the yard directly behind the existing home. Additionally, staff found that five FOUR variances for detached accessory buildings have historically been approved within the surrounding neighborhood, demonstrating that similar relief has previously been determined to be appropriate under comparable circumstances. Granting the requested variance would allow reasonable use of the property while maintaining the character of the neighborhood and would provide substantial justice by treating the property consistently with similarly situated properties. (b) Extraordinary Circumstances – Due to the topography and width of the lot, the rear corner is the most feasible location for the proposed building without requiring extensive excavation or placing the building directly behind the existing home and within the center of the yard. (c) Public Safety and Welfare – The granting of the variance will not impair an adequate supply of light and air to adjacent property or unreasonably increase the congestion in public streets, or increase the danger of fire. (d) Impact on Surrounding Neighborhood – The proposed variance would have little or no impact on the appropriate development, continued use, or value of adjacent properties and the surrounding neighborhood. Recommended Conditions If the Zoning Board of Appeals grants the variance requests, staff recommends the following conditions be placed on the approval. 1. The structure shall be guttered with downspouts. Background The following is a brief summary of the background information we have on file: • • • • Per Township Records, the home was built in 1965. The parcel is serviced by well & municipal grinder pump. See Assessing Record Card. The grinder location has been reviewed by the Utility Director Summary: The applicant is requesting a waterfront yard setback to demolish an existing non-conforming home with no garage and build a new home with an attached garage. There is a portion of the attached garage that will encroach into the waterfront yard. The rest of the home meets the 40’ minimum setback. Variance Requests The following is the section of the Zoning Ordinance that the variance is being requested from: Section 3.04.01 Residential Schedule of Area and Bulk Requirements. (LRR District) Table 3.04.02 Shoreline Setback Required Setback from Shoreline or Ordinary High-Water Mark of a Lake* Condition Principal Building Sites connected to public sewer in Lakeshore Resort Residential Dist. Single Family Home SETBACK PROPOSED SETBACK VARIANCE REQUEST Minimum 40 feet or consistent with the setbacks of adjacent principal buildings, whichever is greater as determined by the Zoning Administrator. If the setbacks of adjacent principal buildings vary because of irregular shoreline, the setback shall be the average of all lots within 500 feet along the shoreline or 40 feet whichever is the greater. Waterfront Setback 40’ 26’ 14’ Summary of Findings of Fact- After reviewing the application and materials provided, I offer the possible findings of fact for your consideration: Please note that in order for a variance to be approved it has to meet all of the standards in 23.05.03. (a) Practical Difficulty/Substantial Justice – The property's peninsula configuration and waterfront surrounding the entire parcel creates an unusual building envelope that is not typical of properties in LRR. The Ordinance recognizes the unique development constraints within this district by allowing reduced side-yard setbacks of 5 feet and 10 feet for other homes; however, this property is further constrained because all yards are waterfront yards. The unique configuration of the property creates a practical difficulty in meeting the required setback while allowing for reasonable development of the parcel. Granting this variance would support substantial justice and is necessary for the preservation and enjoyment of a substantial property right similar to that possessed by other properties in the same vicinity of the subject parcel. (b) Extraordinary Circumstances – The extraordinary circumstance is the unique configuration of the lot, which is located on a peninsula and has waterfront surrounding the property. Unlike typical lots in LRR, the subject property has no traditional side or rear yard that can be utilized for development, as all yard areas are subject to the waterfront setback requirement. The proposed home has been designed to meet the waterfront setback to the greatest extent practical, with the requested variance limited to a small portion of the attached garage. This request was not self-created. The applicant’s architect has worked with staff to determine least amount necessary. (c) Public Safety and Welfare – The granting of the variance will not impair an adequate supply of light and air to adjacent property or unreasonably increase the congestion in public streets, or increase the danger of fire. (d) Impact on Surrounding Neighborhood – The proposed variance would have little or no impact on the appropriate development, continued use, or value of adjacent properties and the surrounding neighborhood. text: GENOA CHARTER TOWNSHIP PLANNING COMMISSION PUBLIC HEARING OCTOBER 13, 2026 - TUESDAY 6:30 P.M. AGENDA CALL TO ORDER: PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: APPROVAL OF AGENDA: DECLARATION OF CONFLICT OF INTEREST: CALL TO THE PUBLIC Non-Agenda Items Only): (Note: The Board reserves the right to not begin new business after 10:00 p.m.) OPEN PUBLIC HEARING # 1… Consideration of an environmental impact assessment and site plan for a proposed parking lot expansion for Schultz Outfitters. The property is located at 5776 East Grand River Avenue, south side of Grand River Avenue west of Dorr Road. The request is petitioned by MITTS LLC. A. Recommendation of Environmental Impact Assessment (8-19-26) B. Disposition of Site Plan (9-18-26) OPEN PUBLIC HEARING # 2… Consideration of an environmental impact assessment and site plan for a proposed parking lot expansion and site improvements for Jonna’s Market. The property is located at 4986 Chilson Road, northwest corner of Chilson and Brighton Roads. The request is petitioned by Mike Jonna. A. Disposition of Environmental Impact Assessment (9-15-26) B. Recommendation of Site Plan (9-15-26) ADMINISTRATIVE BUSINESS: • Staff Report • Approval of September 14, 2026 Planning Commission meeting minutes • Member discussion • Adjournment *Citizen’s Comments- In addition to providing the public with an opportunity to address the Township Board at the beginning of the meeting, opportunity to comment on individual agenda items may be offered by the Chairman as they are presented. Anyone speaking on an agenda item will be limited to 2 minutes. 9 additonal parking spaces are proposed as well as 8 banked parking spaces to meet zoning ordinance requirements for parking. A dumpster enclosure is proposed for the southeast corner of the site. Genoa Township Zoning Board of Appeals Meeting September 15, 2026 Unapproved Minutes Mr. Michael Prudhomme stated he is requesting a variance due to the topography of his yard. If he was to meet the setbacks, it would require extensive excavation and tree removal and put the structure within 25 feet of his house. Ms. Kreutzberg asked if a survey has been done. Mr. Prudhomme stated there are markers on the property, but he cannot say that they are exact. He believes if they are not, they are off by inches. Mr. Rockwell reviewed previous variance requests for accessory structures in this neighborhood. Two of them were withdrawn, one was denied, and two were approved for smaller structures and due to the locations of the well and septics. The request is supposed to be the least amount necessary. The applicant is requesting large variances. Ms. Aulette stated there are at least five approved variances in this neighborhood. Mr. Prudhomme stated he cannot meet the rear yard setback. He can move it further toward the front but will still need a variance. This would not disturb the neighbors because there are large pines and this location is lower than the adjacent properties. Mr. Fons agrees that this is the ideal location on the site to put the structure; however, it does not meet the township’s ordinance. The call to the public was made at 7:15 pm. Mr. Peter Kula of 3796 Kipling owns the house behind Mr. Prudhomme. He stated there is a lot of property in his backyard. He will see it from his house if it is put where it is being proposed. He is the president of the homeowner’s association and their requirements are that the structure must be 12 x 12 minimum and the board has to approve the architecture. The call to the public was closed at 7:17 pm. Mr. Prudhomme reiterated that moving the structure further toward the front would be very close to his house and at a higher elevation. The location he has proposed is much lower. It would not be an eyesore. Keeping equipment outside would be an eyesore. Moved by Kreutzberg, supported by Rockwell to table Case #26-15 for Michael Prudhomme until the October 20, 2026 ZBA meeting, at the applicant’s request. The motion carried unanimously. 3. 26-16…A request by Mitts LLC, 5776 E. Grand River, for a side yard setback variance and any other variances deemed necessary by the Zoning Board of Appeals, for parking lot expansion. Mr. Chris Grzenkowicz, the design engineer, provided a review of the property and the proposed project. They are requesting an eight-foot side-yard variance. There are nine parking spaces, which is sufficient for this business; however, the ordinance requires 23 spaces for this use. Parking cannot be put in the front of the property due to the setback requirements. They are proposing to make one driveway going in only and one going out only and add parking 3 Genoa Township Zoning Board of Appeals Meeting September 15, 2026 Unapproved Minutes spaces to each of those drives. They are proposing to bank parking spaces to avoid taking down trees. They also need to meet the Brighton Fire Authority’s requirement for turning radius. He noted that all uses that are permitted, and those that require a special use at this property, would require a variance to meet the parking requirement. Chairperson McCreary stated that if the fire department agrees with this, then she does also. Mr. Grzenkowicz stated that 60 percent of their business is online, with only 40 percent at the store. Mr. Soucy stated the proposed use compliments the other businesses in the area. He does not see any issues with this request. Mr. Fons agrees. The call to the public was made at 7:42 pm with no response. Moved by Rockwell, supported by Soucy, to approve Case #26-15 for Mitts, LLC for 5776 East Grand River, for a side yard variance of 8 feet from the required 10 feet for a side yard setback of 2 feet, to allow for additional parking, based on the following findings of fact: • Strict compliance with the ordinance would prevent the applicant from having enough parking for the use. Granting of the requested variance does provide substantial justice or a substantial property right similar to that possessed by other businesses in this zoning district. • The subject property possesses an irregular and angled lot configuration, with an existing principal structure occupying a substantial portion of the parcel. The relationship between the existing building, property boundaries, access points, and required vehicle circulation results in a limited usable area for parking. Strict application of the required side-yard setback would substantially reduce the functional parking area and would create practical difficulties in maintaining reasonable access and circulation on the site. These conditions are peculiar to the physical configuration and existing development of the property and are not the result of the applicant's actions. This issue is not self-created. • The granting of the variance will not impair an adequate supply of light and air to adjacent property or unreasonably increase the congestion in public streets or increase the danger of fire. Further, relocating these spaces out to two feet from the property line creates parking spaces that do not encroach into the Brighton Area Fire Departments clear turning radius. • The proposed variance would have little or no impact on the appropriate development, continued use or value of adjacent properties and the surrounding neighborhood. This approval is conditioned upon the following: 1. Applicant must obtain Site Plan Approval through Planning Commission. 2. Applicant must close off connection to the adjacent property at 5796 Grand River. 3. No outside sales or storage in the lot. The motion carried unanimously. Administrative Business: 1. Approval of minutes for the August 18, 2026 Zoning Board of Appeals meeting. Moved by Kreutzberg, supported by Soucy, to approve the minutes of the August 18, 2026 Zoning Board of Appeals meeting as submitted. The motion carried unanimously. 4 Genoa Township Zoning Board of Appeals Meeting September 15, 2026 Unapproved Minutes 2. Correspondence Ms. Aulette stated there will be one new case on next month’s agenda. 3. Member Discussion Mr. Soucy stated absentee ballots will be mailed out next week. The board discussed having previous similar variance requests included in the packet. 4. Adjournment Moved by Fons, supported by Kreutzberg, to adjourn the meeting at 7:52 pm. The motion carried unanimously. Respectfully submitted: Patty Thomas, Recording Secretary 5 September 29, 2026 Planning Commission Genoa Township 2911 Dorr Road Brighton, Michigan 48116 Attention: Subject: Location: Zoning: Amy Ruthig, Planning Director Schultz Outfitters – Site Plan Review #2 5776 East Grand River Avenue – south side of Grand River Avenue, west of Dorr Road GCD General Commercial District Dear Commissioners: At the Township’s request, we have reviewed the revised submittal requesting site plan review and approval for a new retail use in the existing commercial building at 5776 East Grand River Avenue (cover sheet dated 9/18/26). A. Summary 1. The applicant requests Commission approval of banked parking based on a high ratio of online business (as opposed to in-person). 2. The Commission may allow the proposed evergreen trees in the required greenbelt (or may require the use of canopy trees). 3. The Commission may modify landscaping requirements, per Section 12.02.13. 4. The Commission may allow the proposed location of the waste receptacle and enclosure (rear yard with a 1’ side setback). 5. The applicant must address any site plan comments provided by the Township Engineering and/or Brighton Area Fire Authority. B. Proposal/Process The applicant requests review and approval of a new retail business within an existing commercial building, as well as site improvements including additional parking, a new waste receptacle/enclosure, and additional landscaping. Per Table 7.02 of the Township Zoning Ordinance, retail establishments with up to 15,000 square feet of gross floor area are permitted by right in the GCD (with no associated use requirements). Procedurally, the Planning Commission has review and approval authority over the site plan but must put forth a recommendation to the Township Board on the Environmental Impact Assessment. www.safebuilt.com Genoa Township Planning Commission Schultz Outfitters Site Plan Review #2 Page 2 Subject site Aerial view of site and surroundings (looking south) C. 1. Site Plan Review Dimensional Requirements. As a previously developed site, there are limited impacts on the dimensional requirements of the GCD. However, the project does include new parking spaces and additional impervious surface. The proposed parking spaces on the east side of the site do not meet the required 10’ setback; however, a variance was recently granted by the ZBA. (The applicant has added a note to Sheet SP1 stating such.) Additionally, the slight increase in impervious surface remains compliant with the GCD maximum (75% allowed; 71.2% proposed). 2. Building Design and Materials. The applicant has confirmed that no exterior building modifications are proposed at this time. 3. Pedestrian Circulation. The site currently has a public sidewalk along Grand River Avenue, as well as a connection to the sidewalk along the front of the building. 4. Vehicular Circulation. The site currently has 2 curb cuts, and the proposal entails a one-way circulation pattern (counterclockwise). Drive aisles are of sufficient width for one-way circulation around the property. The applicant must address any comments provided by the Township Engineer and/or the Brighton Area Fire Authority with respect to vehicular circulation. 5. Parking. Based on the parking calculations included on Sheet SP1, the project requires 23 parking spaces. The site plan provides 18 parking spaces, including 1 barrier-free space. The proposal includes banked parking for 8 additional spaces, with a net gain of 5 to bring the site into compliance. The applicant requests the use of banked parking in accordance with Section 14.02.05 because 60% of their business is conducted online. Genoa Township Planning Commission Schultz Outfitters Site Plan Review #2 Page 3 The design and dimensions of parking spaces and drive aisles comply with Ordinance standards. While we do not typically advise the use of parallel parking spaces for commercial uses, the site layout will not allow perpendicular or angled parking on either side. Lastly, the 2 parallel spaces closest to the rear of the site – 1 banked space on the west side and 1 proposed space on the east side – will be difficult to navigate given how tight the area around the spaces will be (the space on the east side abuts the waste receptacle enclosure). However, these spaces do meet dimensional requirements for parallel parking spaces. 6. Exterior Lighting. Our understanding is that no exterior lighting modifications are proposed. 7. Landscaping. The landscape plan has been reviewed for compliance with the standards of Section 12.02, as follows: Standard Greenbelt Required 20’ width 4 trees Buffer Zone C (E) 10’ width 11 trees OR 44 shrubs Buffer Zone C (W) 10’ width 11 trees OR 44 shrubs 10’ width 8 trees OR 32 shrubs 10.7’ width 11 existing trees 24 shrubs 5’ width 32 shrubs 180 SF landscaped area 2 trees 261 SF landscaped area 1 existing tree 1 proposed tree Buffer Zone C (S) Parking Lot Proposed 2 existing trees 2 evergreen trees 28 shrubs 2’ width 2 trees 4 shrubs Comments In compliance (PC may allow up to 50% evergreen trees) ZBA variance mitigates deficient width; PC may modify requirements accordingly, per 12.02.13 In compliance Plantings in compliance; width is an existing condition that PC may allow to remain In compliance 8. Waste Receptacle. The proposed waste receptacle has been reviewed for compliance with the standards of Section 12.04, as follows: Location Access Base design Enclosure Requirement Proposed Comments Rear yard or non-required side yard AND not less than 20’ from residential Clear access w/ out damaging buildings/vehicles 9’ x 9’ concrete pad (minimum) w/ 6’ extension 3-sided enclosure w/ gate Masonry walls 6’ height/taller than receptacle Rear yard 1’ side setback Yard location is compliant; PC may allow side encroachment, per 12.04.02 Requirement met Sufficient access 9’ x 15’ concrete pad Requirement met 3 sides w/ gate across 4th Masonry walls 6’ Requirements met Should you have any questions concerning this matter, please do not hesitate to contact our office. Respectfully, SAFEBUILT Brian V. Borden, AICP Planning Manager October 5, 2026 Ms. Amy Ruthig Genoa Township 2911 Dorr Road Brighton, MI 48116 Re: Schultz Outfitters Site Plan Review No. 2 Dear Ms. Ruthig: Tetra Tech conducted a review of the site plan submittal for Schultz Outfitters last dated September 18, 2026 . The site plan was prepared by Desine Inc on behalf of Mitts LLC. The development is located on 0.74 acres south of Grand River Avenue 1,000 feet west of Dorr Road. The Petitioner is proposing a parking lot expansion. The proposed site includes pavement improvements and a new dumpster enclosure. We have reviewed the revised site plan, and the petitioner has satisfactorily addressed our previous comments. We have no further engineering related concern with the proposed site plan. Please call or email if you have any questions. INTRODUCTION (Sec. 18.07.01) This impact assessment has been prepared pursuant to Article 18 – SITE PLAN REVIEW of the Zoning Ordinance for the Township of Genoa, Livingston County, Michigan. This Impact Assessment has been prepared under the direction of Christopher A. Grzenkowicz, P.E., DESINE INC., 2183 Pless Drive, Brighton, Michigan 48114. Mr. Grzenkowicz is a licensed Civil Engineer, providing professional engineering services in Livingston County since 1995 with experience in private and municipal development including projects within Genoa Township and Livingston County. B. SITE LOCATION / DESCRIPTION (Sec. 18.07.02) The project site is located on the south side of Grand River Avenue, west of Dorr Road, as shown on Figure 1. The site is an existing parcel containing 0.74 acres of property, bordered on the North by Grand River Avenue, on the East by Wonderland Marine West, with Crystal Gardens banquet center to the South and West. A portion of the building will be utilized as warehouse space for online sales while the remainder of the building will serve as retail space for in person sales. Surface runoff is medium, permeability is moderately low and the soil erosion hazard is light. The current moratorium was established to provide the Township sufficient time to complete the update of the Master Plan and Future Land Use Map and to ensure that future zoning decisions are consistent with the Township's long-term planning policies. The adopted resolution specifically provides that the Board may, by resolution, extend the moratorium one time for a period not to exceed six additional months when necessary to complete the Master Plan, including the Future Land Use Map. As part of the ongoing Master Plan update, the Township had conducted a comprehensive community survey and town hall forums to gather public input regarding future land use, development, and community priorities. Following the presentation and discussion of the survey results, a few residents raised concerns regarding whether the intent of certain survey questions was clearly understood by those responding to the survey. Specifically, questions were raised as to whether some of the responses may have reflected differing interpretations of what particular questions were intended to ask. The Planning Commission believes additional public input would be beneficial to clarify a few of the responses received through the original survey. The additional six months would allow the Township to conduct this follow-up public engagement, provide residents and property owners with an additional opportunity to clarify their preferences, evaluate the resulting information, and appropriately incorporate that input into the Master Plan and Future Land Use Map. This additional time will help ensure that the final documents reflect a thorough public engagement process and provide clear guidance for future land use and zoning decisions. WHEREAS, on October 6, 2025, the Township Board adopted Resolution No. 251006B (the “Original Resolution”), establishing a temporary moratorium, pursuant to Section 21.06.03 of the Zoning Ordinance, on the review and approval of rezoning applications in order to allow for updates to the Master Plan and Future Land Use Map within Genoa Charter Township; and WHEREAS, the Original Resolution provided that the moratorium would remain in effect for a period of twelve (12) months from its effective date, or until an updated Master Plan and Future Land Use Map becomes effective, whichever occurs first, and that the Township Board may, by resolution, extend the moratorium one time for a period not to exceed six (6) additional months, if necessary to complete the updated Master Plan and Future Land Use Map; and WHEREAS, Section 21.06.03 of the Zoning Ordinance authorizes the Township Board to impose a temporary moratorium for a period of up to twelve (12) months, and further authorizes a one-time extension of up to six (6) additional months by resolution; and WHEREAS, as part of the Master Plan update process, the Township conducted a community survey to gather public input regarding future land use, development, and community priorities; and WHEREAS, following the presentation and discussion of the survey results, a few residents raised concerns regarding whether the intent of certain survey questions was clearly understood by those responding to the survey and whether certain responses may have reflected differing interpretations of the questions presented; and WHEREAS, the Planning Commission has determined that additional public input would be beneficial to clarify certain responses received through the original community survey and to better understand the preferences and priorities of Township residents and property owners; and WHEREAS, additional time is necessary to conduct this follow-up public engagement, provide residents and property owners with an additional opportunity to clarify their preferences, evaluate the resulting information, and appropriately incorporate that information into the Master Plan and Future Land Use Map; and Packet Page 11 WHEREAS, the Township Board finds that completing this additional public engagement before finalizing the Master Plan and Future Land Use Map will help ensure that the final documents reflect a thorough planning process and provide clear guidance for future land use and zoning decisions; and WHEREAS, the Township Board therefore finds that a one-time six (6) month extension of the existing moratorium is reasonable and necessary to allow the Township to complete the additional public engagement and Master Plan update process. This extension does not exceed the six (6) month maximum extension period authorized under Section 21.06.03 of the Zoning Ordinance; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1) The temporary moratorium established by Resolution No. 251006B on the review and approval of rezoning applications in order to allow for updates to the Master Plan and Future Land Use Map within Genoa Charter Township; is hereby extended for an additional period of six (6) months, pursuant to Section 21.06.03 of the Zoning Ordinance. 2) This extension shall commence immediately upon the expiration of the initial twelve-month moratorium period and shall remain in effect for six (6) additional months thereafter, or until a Master Plan and Future Land Use map update is effective, whichever occurs first. This is the one-time extension authorized under Section 21.06.03 of the Zoning Ordinance, and the moratorium shall not be further extended beyond the period set forth herein. 3) All other terms, conditions, definitions, and exceptions set forth in Resolution No. 251006B, shall remain in full force and effect and are hereby ratified and incorporated by reference. 4) The provisions of this Resolution are severable. If any provision, clause, or part is declared invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions shall not be affected and shall remain in full force and effect. 5) Notice of this Resolution shall be published within seven (7) days of its adoption. The notice must include a summary of the Resolution's effect, the length of the extension, and where the public may inspect the Resolution enacting the extension. 6) This Resolution shall become effective immediately following publication. Invocation Supervisor Spicher led the invocation for the Board and the members of the public. Pledge of Allegiance The Pledge of Allegiance was recited. Roll Call The following members were present constituting a quorum for the transaction of business: Kevin Spicher, Candie Hovarter, Robin Hunt, Bill Reiber, Rick Soucy, Jodi Valenti, and Todd Walker. Also present was Township Manager Kelly VanMarter and five people in the audience. Call to the Public The call to the public was opened at 6:31 pm. Mr. Jeff Dhaenens of 5494 Sharp Drive hopes that if the moratorium is approved this evening, there will be an opportunity to allow for a reasonable conversation to happen. There are projects coming up that personally affect him and he cannot do anything until the Master Plan is complete. The call to the public was closed at 6:33 pm. Approval of Consent Agenda: Moved by Soucy, supported by Walker, to approve the consent agenda as presented. The motion carried unanimously. 1. Payment of Bills: October 5, 2026 2. Request to approve the September 21, 2026 regular meeting minutes. 1 Packet Page 8 Genoa Charter Township Board Meeting October 5, 2026 Unapproved Minutes Approval of Regular Agenda Moved by Hunt, supported by Valenti, to approve the regular agenda as presented. The motion carried unanimously. 3. Consideration of Resolution 261005 for a six-month extension of the Temporary Moratorium on the review and approval of rezoning applications in order to allow for updates to the Master Plan and Future Land Use Map. (Roll Call) Ms. VanMarter stated the Planning Commission has requested staff to reach out to some of the residents who filled out the survey to ask them for more clarification on how they responded to certain questions. Mr. Reiber questioned if the people who were going to be contacted were people who did not fill out the survey completely. Ms. VanMarter stated they will be contacting everyone who provided an email address to ask them if they correctly understood the questions regarding the South Latson Area. Ms. Hunt stated this is an important issue and it is worth adding an additional six months to the moratorium. Mr. Walker stated it is best to get it right. It was noted this moratorium cannot be extended past these additional six months. Moved by Soucy, supported by Hovarter, to approve Resolution 261005 for a six-month extension of the Temporary Moratorium on the acceptance, review, processing, and approval of rezoning applications as authorized by Resolution 251006B to provide additional time for public engagement and clarification of the previous community survey results and to complete the updated of the Township Master Plan and future Land Use Map. The motion carried unanimously with a roll call vote. (Reiber – yes; Hunt – yes; Valenti – yes; Hovarter – yes; Walker – yes; Soucy – yes; Spicher – yes) Member Updates Mr. Reiber asked if there was a pre-planning meeting with Peacemakers. Ms. VanMarter stated it was held last week. Mr. Reiber stated he advised that he was very interested in attending that meeting and he was not sent any documentation or meeting link. Ms. VanMarter will provide information from that meeting to Mr. Reiber. Mr. Walker stated BAFA will be discussing grants they have been awarded at their next meeting. Board Comments Mr. Soucy stated the clerk’s office mailed 6,299 absentee ballots. Mr. Reiber asked on the status of the 77 acre parcel that is owned by the township. Supervisor Spicher stated they have been reviewing and applying for grants. Mr. Reiber asked when the additional baseline data will be collected for the noise ordinance. 2 Packet Page 9 Genoa Charter Township Board Meeting October 5, 2026 Unapproved Minutes Ms. VanMarter stated staff is working with the township attorney on the contract. Mr. Reiber asked for an update on the wage study. Ms. VanMarter stated staff has received a draft of the study and she is providing feedback regarding formatting and typographical errors to the contractor. They are gathering and obtaining additional data. Ms. VanMarter stated the first meeting in November has been canceled due to the election. Adjournment Moved by Walker, supported by Valenti, to adjourn the meeting at 6:59 pm. The motion carried unanimously. Respectfully Submitted, Patty Thomas Recording Secretary Approved: Rick Soucy, Clerk Genoa Charter Township Kevin Spicher, Supervisor Genoa Charter Township 3 Packet Page 10 0EMORANDUM TO: Honorable Board of Trustees FROM: Amy Ruthig, Planning Director DATE: October 15, 2026 RE: Schultz Outfitters Parking Lot Improvements 5796 E. Grand River Avenue (11-10-400-007) Environmental Impact Assessment Please find attached the project case file for Schultz Outfitters. This project involves a new retail business within an existing commercial building including additional parking, waste receptacle/enclosure, and landscaping. The property is located at 5776 E. Grand River, south side of Grand River Avenue, west of Dorr Road. The request is petitioned by Mitts, LLC. The property is zoned General Commercial District (GCD). Subject Property The proposed retail business is a permitted use. In order to allow for the new business, additional parking is required per the Zoning Ordinance. In order to proceed, the applicant was required to obtain Zoning Board of Appeals approval for a parking lot side yard setback which was received at the September 15, 2026 meeting. The Planning Commission is to put forth a recommendation to the Township Board on the environmental impact assessment and deposition of the site plan. The project was heard before the Planning Commission on October 13, 2026 and the Commission recommended approval of the environmental impact assessment and approved the site plan. Based on the recommendation from the Planning Commission I offer the following for your consideration: Packet Page 11 ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT Moved by ___, supported by ___ to APPROVE the Environmental Impact Assessment dated August 19, 2026 for proposed parking lot expansion and site improvements for Schultz Outfitters located at 5776 E. Grand River Avenue with the following conditions: 1. Outdoor storage, sales or displays is prohibited. 2. The entrance and exit signs shall comply with the township’s sign ordinance. If you should have any questions, please feel free to contact me. Best Regards, Amy Ruthig Planning Director Packet Page 12 9 additonal parking spaces are proposed as well as 8 banked parking spaces to meet zoning ordinance requirements for parking. A dumpster enclosure is proposed for the southeast corner of the site.
