title: Merged documents for October 14, 2026 Board Meeting
text: Williamstown Township Township Board Meeting Minutes September 30, 2026 Call to Order The Williamstown Township Board of Trustees held their regular meeting at 6:30 p.m. on September 30, 2026. Supervisor Poth called the meeting to order and Trustee Steinberg led the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll Call Present: Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland, Treasurer VanErp, Trustee Brinker, Trustee Creagh, and Trustee Steinberg. Approval of Agenda Motion by Trustee Brinker, second by Trustee Creagh to approve the agenda. Discussion: None. Motion passed. Public Comment for agenda or non-agenda items Opened at 6:33 PM None. Closed at 6:33 PM Consent Agenda Trustee Brinker moved to approve the consent agenda, as presented, consisting of: • • Approve the minutes of the August 12, 2026 meeting. General Fund Accounts Payable Paid #1, check numbers 32852-32866, for a total of $21,816.62 and Accounts Payable Paid #2, check numbers 32876-32882. • General Fund Accounts Payable for Approval #1, check numbers 32867-32875, for a total of $11,410.98. Second by: Trustee Creagh Discussion: None Roll Call Vote: Ayes: Treasurer VanErp, Trustee Brinker, Trustee Creagh, Trustee Steinberg, Supervisor Poth, and Clerk Cleveland. Nays: None Motion Passed. ACTION ITEMS Treasurer VanErp moved the Williamstown Township Board enter closed session pursuant to MCL 15.268(1)(h) to discuss a confidential legal opinion with Township legal counsel regarding the Natural Burial Section of Summit Cemetery. Second by Trustee Brinker. Board of Trustees Meeting 9-30-2026 Page 1 of 4 Roll Call Vote of 2/3rds elected and serving: Ayes: Trustee Brinker, Trustee Creagh, Trustee Steinberg, Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland, and Treasurer VanErp. Nays: None Discussion: None Motion Passed. The Board adjourned into Closed Session at 6:36 p.m. The Board reconvened at 7:31 p.m. Trustee Creagh moved to exit closed session and re-open the public portion of the Township Board Meeting. Second by: Trustee Brinker Motion Passed. Green Cemetery Trustee Brinker moved the Williamstown Township Board approve an ordinance and resolution enacting a temporary moratorium for a period of up to 12 months, subject to extension by resolution, on the sale, reservation, and transfer of all new green burial spaces within the Natural Burial Section of Summit Cemetery, while honoring rights of burial purchased before the effective date of this moratorium. Second by: Trustee Creagh Discussion: None Roll Call Vote: Ayes: Trustee Steinberg, Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland, Treasurer VanErp, Trustee Brinker, and Trustee Creagh. Nays: None Motion Passed. Clerk Cleveland moved to enter closed session pursuant to MCL 15.6281(h) to discuss a confidential legal opinion with Township legal counsel regarding the ITC Line Opposition Landowners Membership Group Agreement. Second by: Trustee Creagh Roll Call Vote of 2/3rds elected and serving: Ayes: Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland, Treasurer VanErp, Trustee Creagh, Trustee Brinker, and Trustee Steinberg. Nays: None Motion Passed. The Board adjourned into Closed Session at 7:36 p.m. The Board reconvened at 8:14 p.m. Board of Trustees Meeting 9-30-2026 Page 2 of 4 Clerk Cleveland moved to exit closed session and re-open the public portion of the Township Board meeting. Second by: Treasurer VanErp Motion passed. WLCAA Membership Trustee Creagh moved the Williamstown Township Board, based on advice from legal counsel, does not approve joining the WLCCA membership, at this time. Second by: Treasurer VanErp Discussion: None Roll Call Vote: Ayes: Clerk Cleveland, Treasurer VanErp, Trustee Brinker, Trustee Creagh, Trustee Steinberg, and Supervisor Poth. Nays: None Motion Passed. Trustee Creagh moved the Williamstown Township Board direct the Township Supervisor to meet with the WLCCA legal counsel to explore potential opportunities of collaboration and cooperation on the ITC corridor expansion. Second: Trustee Brinker Discussion: None. Roll Call Vote: Ayes: Treasurer VanErp, Trustee Brinker, Trustee Creagh, Trustee Steinberg, Supervisor Poth, and Clerk Cleveland. Nays: None Motion Passed. Truck Route Policy Clerk Cleveland moved the Williamstown Township Board approve the Truck Route Ordinance as amended. Second by: Trustee Steinberg Discussion: None. Roll Call Vote: Ayes: Trustee Brinker, Trustee Creagh, Trustee Steinberg, Supervisor Poth, Clerk Cleveland, and Treasurer VanErp. Nays: None Motion Passed. Board of Trustees Meeting 9-30-2026 Page 3 of 4 Discussion Items Article 8 Review – The Board discussed clarification on defining a drive-thru and kennel regulations. Reports – Departments and Committees Supervisor’s Report – Supervisor Poth updated the Board on his recent meeting with the lead engineer for C2AE regarding the upcoming renovation plans at the Community Park. Moving forward, a Zoom meeting is planned regarding the process and plan moving forward. Williamston City is supportive of seeking a date in January to meet. Mr. Poth asked the Board to think about items for the agenda and topics to discuss for this meeting. NIESA – No report. Parks Committee – Trustee Steinberg noted that he will be assisting with the upcoming Harvest Festival. Concern regarding the current state of the Community Park Sign. It is no longer level. The installer will be contacted. Elections/Clerk – Clerk Cleveland reported on upcoming election progress. She is encouraging residents to return their ballot as soon as possible. Early voting begins October 24th through November 1st. Cemetery – No report. Roads – Supervisor Poth noted that the completion of Thatcher Rd. will occur soon. This is the last township road repair for 2026. In total, approximately $76,000 was spent on road maintenance this year. Branch School – Sixty-six bowls of ice cream were served, and one antique car was on display at the recent Ice Cream Social on September 13th. German Exchange students and teachers recently toured the City and the school. Mr. Mitch Lutzke shared information about the history of Branch School with the visitors. Public comment for agenda and non-agenda items Opened at 8:47PM None. Closed at 8:47PM Next Meeting: Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 6:30 pm Adjournment and Review Trustee Creagh moved to adjourn the meeting. Second by Trustee Brinker. Meeting adjourned at 8:48 PM. text: AGENDA WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP PLANNING COMMISSION October 13, 2026 6:30 p.m. CALL TO ORDER PLEDGE OF ALLEGIENCE ROLL CALL APPROVAL OF AGENDA APPROVAL OF MINUTES Minutes of September 26, 2026 PUBLIC COMMENT (Limited to 3 minutes per person) UNFINISHED BUSINESS • Zoning Ordinance Review—Phase 7 Review of drafts of the following Articles: o o o o o o o o o o o o o o Article 10 Article 11 Article 12 Article 13 Article 14 Article 15 Article 16 Version 2 Article 17 Article 18 Article 19 Article 20 Article 21 Article 22 Excerpt from Article 8 NEW BUSINESS • Farmland and Open Space Preservation Program Application, Aaron Jorgensen North side of Sherwood Road, west of Branch Road (PIN# 33-03-03-21-451-005) Planning Commission Agenda October 13, 2026 Page 1 of 2 Consider making a recommendation to the Township Board to approve or deny the application for a Farmland and Open Space Preservation Application. • Memorandum from Ken Skunda, Code Enforcement to the Planning Commission Proposed Ordinance Language - Shipping Containers and Portable Storage Units (PODs)—For discussion. PLANNING AND BOARD REPORTS Township Board Planning Commission Chair Planning Commissioners Planning Staff CORRESPONDENCE None PUBLIC COMMENT (Limited to 3 minutes per person) REVIEW ADJOURNMENT Note: Next meeting is scheduled for Tuesday, November 10th, 2026 Planning Commission Agenda October 13, 2026 Page 2 of 2 WILLIAMSTOWN TOWNSHIP PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES September 23, 2026 CALL TO ORDER The Williamstown Township Planning Commission convened at 6:30 pm at the Township Hall, 4990 Zimmer Road, Williamston, MI. Chair Eidt called the meeting to order. Chair Eidt led the group in the Pledge of Allegiance. PRESENT: Chair Eidt, Commissioners Mark, Porter, Tocarchick, Thorp and Trustee Creagh. ABSENT: Commissioner Weston, Cutshaw, and Flore. Quorum established. ALSO PRESENT: Planning Consultant Chris Doozan of McKenna and Sheryl Monette, Planning Assistant. APPROVAL OF AGENDA Motion by Mark second by Porter to approve the amended agenda with the addition of Red Cedar Bend Apartments under New Business and the CIP (Capital Improvement Plan) under Planning and Board Reports with the Planning Staff. Motion approved 6-0. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Motion by Porter, second by Creagh to approve the Meeting Minutes for 8/26/2026. Motion approved 6-0. PUBLIC COMMENT Opened at 6:32 pm None Closed at 6:32 pm SPECIAL TOPIC Practical Application and Nuances of Ordinance Enforcement Ken Skunda, Code Enforcement Officer, reviewed the difference between complaint-based code enforcement and patrol-based code enforcement with the Planning Commission. He discussed some challenges he is having with the current language regarding shipping containers in the 1 Ordinances. Mr. Skunda stated that when he has feedback or concerns regarding language in an ordinance or an ordinance itself that he discusses it with the Township Supervisor and the Planning Assistant. UNFINISHED BUSINESS Data Center Regulations Chris Doozan, Planning Consultant, reviewed his September 1st letter to the Planning Commission regarding Updated Zoning Revisions Regarding Data Centers. Mr. Doozan stated he has reviewed both the City of Williamston’s ordinance and the MTA’s sample ordinance. He reviewed the new revisions to Data Center Ordinance and some edits were made. The Planning Commission asked that Mr. Doozan review the sound standard (45 versus 55) and vibration standard. Questions were asked if there is any vibration damping equipment that should be included in the ordinance and if it would be possible to find out what the levels for sound and tonal/vibrations were coming in for complaints on an existing hyperscale data centers (possibly in Dowagiac). Mr. Doozan stated that he would do further research. The Planning Commission discussed the need for the ordinance to be reviewed by the Township Attorney. Motion by Creagh, second by Mark, to postpone action on the Data Center regulations until the November 10th meeting to allow for revision and review by the Township Attorney. Motion approved 6- 0. NEW BUSINESS Barkham Creek Farms Site Plan Review Chris Doozan, Planning Consultant, reviewed his September 10th letter to the Planning Commission regarding Barkham Creek Farm Site Plan Review- Site Plan Dated 8/30/2026. It was noted that no other property on Haslett Road is curbed and guttered. Paving the apron of the driveway is needed for safety. Mr. Doozan reviewed that if the barn is to be used as an event barn, a separate Special Land Use Permit and Site Plan Review would be needed. Mr. Barkham addressed the Planning Commission. He stated the barn needed to be moved to accommodate a second driveway that was needed for safety reasons. To comply with the Ingham County Road Department’s requirements the new driveway came in where the barn was located. Consequently, they decided to move and preserve the barn. Mr. Barkham stated that barn will be used for organizing school field trips, church fundraising or his wife’s parties. Mr. Barkham stated that the barn would not be rented out for any events. He stated that even though the barn will have bathrooms they will continue to use porta johns on site as they have in the past. Hours of operation are 10 am to 6 pm and the business is open for six weeks out of the year ending on October 31st. He stated there is lighting on the cider mill and that lighting has not been an issue in the past. Mr. Barkham stated that in addition to the dumpster noted on the 2 site plan that there are trash receptacles throughout the property and by the cider mill. These are emptied daily. Mr. Barkham stated that the asphalt paving of the driveway aprons would not be complete until next year due to timing. Mr. Barkham stated that there wasn’t enough distance between a utility pole and a tree to accommodate the 31 feet width for the east driveway. Discussion ensued. It was determined that Mr. Barkham would need to apply to the Zoning Board of Appeals for a variance from the requirement for a 31-foot-wide paved driveway to allow a 25foot-wide paved driveway on the east side. Motion by Creagh, second by Porter, to recommend approval of the Barkham Creek Farms Site Plan subject to seeking and receiving a variance from the Zoning Board of Appeals to allow a 25foot-wide paved driveway on the east side. Motion approved 6- 0. Review of Bath Charter Township Comprehensive Plan Commissioner Tocarchick stated that she reviewed Bath Charter Township Comprehensive Plan and that she did not see anything of concern. Red Cedar Bend Apartments Chris Doozan, Planning Consultant, reviewed his September 22nd letter to the Planning Commission regarding Red Cedar Bend Apartments, Planned Development Phase II Review. Discussion ensued regarding the change in plans, which involved the stormwater drainage system. Instead of underground detention, the plans now call for use of the pond in front as a detention pond. The Planning Commission discussed whether a fence was needed around the pond but decided that one was not needed because 1 on 4 side slopes are proposed. No action was taken by the Planning Commission. *Commissioner Tocarchick left meeting at 7:35pm and returned at 7:37 pm. PLANNING AND BOARD REPORTS AND REVIEW Township Board. Trustee Creagh stated at the last Township Board meeting the Board approved an MDOT Resolution for Lothamer 5K Charity Run, selected an engineering & design firm, C2AE, for the Township Park, and amended the Neighborhood Road Policy to address recent changes in funding. The Board also heard from Bethany Barker from Williamstown Locke Corridor Community Alliance regarding their organizing and opposition of the ITC power high-voltage powerlines. Planning Commission Chair. None Planning Staff. Sheryl Monette, Planning Assistant, gave a report from the CIP (Capital Improvement Plan) Subcommittee. Minutes from the September 1st meeting were included in the meeting packet. 3 CORRESPONDENCE: None PUBLIC COMMENT Opened at 7:48 pm Becky Wegar, Township Resident. Ms. Wegar asked if the draft Data Center Ordinance takes in consideration of allowing only close loop systems. Tom Korroch, Township Resident. Mr. Korroch shared with the Planning Commission his desire to build a pond, berms and putting green for his personal use on a property that he purchased behind his primary resident. He stated that he has been in contact with EGLE along with meeting with Sheryl Monette, Planning Assistant, regarding the project. Mr. Korroch voiced concern regarding the cost of the engineering and surveying consultant fees he would need to get through the process with EGLE and potentially the Township. Mr. Korroch stated that he has received 3 quotes ranging from$13,000 to $14,000. Planning Consultant, Chris Doozan offered to meet with Mr. Korroch on September 24th at the Township Hall to review the quotes and to provide further guidance. Closed at 7:59 pm REVIEW Chair Eidt reviewed the Planning Commission’s actions from the meeting: - Approved the meeting minutes 8/26/2026 Heard from Ken Skunda, Code Enforcement Officer. Postponed action on the Data Center Ordinance until November 10th meeting so the Township Attorney can review the Ordinance. Received Commissioner Tocarchick’s review of the Bath Charter Township Comprehensive Plan. ADJOURNMENT Motion by Creagh, second by Tocarchick to adjourn the meeting. Motion approved 6-0 Meeting adjourned at 8:00 PM ___ Sheryl Monette Recording Secretary ___ Donna Tocarchick Planning Commission Secretary 4 September 29, 2026 Planning Commission Williamstown Township 4990 N. Williamston, MI 48895 Subject: Zoning Revisions Involving Articles 10.00 through 22.00 Dear Planning Commissioners: Enclosed for your review are Articles 10.00 through 22.00 of the Zoning Ordinance, which deal with the establishment of zoning districts and the regulations within the zoning districts. As previously discussed, we have extracted the long lists of permitted uses from each zoning district and put them in a comprehensive six-page table, titled Permitted Uses by District. This table can be found in Section 10.07. A consequence of creating this table was the necessity to include additional regulations in Article 8.00. These additional regulations are saved in Section 8.02(UU) through (DDD) and are attached as an Excerpt for your review. These regulations are cross-referenced in the Permitted Uses table. By creating the Permitted Uses by District table, you will note that the district regulations in Articles 11.00 through 22.00 are now condensed to just two pages. The exception to this rule is Article 16.00, the Mobile Home Park District, which must generally comply with Michigan Public Act 96 of 1987, as amended, and the Manufactured Housing Rules (MHRs). If the Township wishes to vary from the MHRs, then it must seek approval for the “higher standard” from the Manufactured Housing Commission. In the enclosed copy of Article 16.00, we have noted in red whether each regulation complies or varies from the current MHRs. We look forward to discussing this with you at the October Planning Commission meeting. Sincerely, McKENNA Christopher J. Doozan, AICP Community Planning Consultant c: Ron Poth, Township Supervisor Sheryl Monette, Planning Assistant ARTICLE 10.00 Establishment of Zoning Districts Section 10.01 Creation of Districts For the purposes of this Ordinance, Williamstown Township is hereby divided into the following Zoning Districts as shown on the Official Zoning Map: Residential Districts R-1 R-1-S RR RE AG-SF RM-1 MHP One-Family Residential Suburban Residential Rural Residential Rural Estates Agricultural Small Farms Multiple-Family Residential Mobile Home Park District Nonresidential Districts AG-C OS-1 B-1 B-2 I-1 GD Commercial Agriculture Office Service Limited Business Commercial Center Light Industrial Green Zone Planned Development District Other Districts MU PD Section 10.02 Mixed Use Overlay District M-43 Corridor Overlay District Planned Development Adoption of Zoning Map The boundaries of the Zoning Districts listed in Section 10.01 are hereby established as shown on the Official Zoning Map of the Township of Williamstown. The Zoning Map with all notations, references, and other information shown thereon shall be, and is hereby declared to be a part of this Ordinance as if fully described herein. In accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance and Michigan Public Act 110 of 2006, as amended, changes made in district boundaries and other matters portrayed on the Zoning Map shall be entered on the Zoning Map after the amendment has been approved by the Township Board and has been published in a newspaper of general circulation in the Township and posted on the Township’s website. No changes of any nature shall be made to the Zoning Map except in conformity with the procedures set forth in Article 29.00 of this Ordinance. Regardless of the existence of copies of the Zoning Map which may, from time to time, be made or published, the official Zoning Map shall be located at the Township Hall and shall be the final authority with regard to the current zoning status of all land in the Township. Williamstown Township Zoning Ordinance Page 10 - 1 Article 10.00 Section 10.03 Establishment of Zoning Districts Interpretation of District Boundaries The following rules shall apply to the interpretation of zoning district boundaries: A. Boundaries indicated as approximately following the center lines of streets, roads, railroad rights-of-way, or alleys shall be construed to follow such center line. B. Boundaries indicated as approximately following platted lot lines shall be construed as following such lot lines. C. Boundaries indicated as approximately following Township limits shall be construed as following such limits. D. Boundaries indicated as approximately following the center lines of streams, rivers, or other bodies of water shall be construed to follow such center lines. E. Boundaries indicated as approximately following the shoreline of a body of water shall be construed to follow such shoreline; in the event of a change in the shoreline, the boundary shall be construed as moving with the actual shoreline. F. Boundaries indicated as parallel to or as an extension of features cited in paragraphs A through E above shall be construed as being parallel to or an extension of the features cited. Distances not specified on the official Zoning Map shall be determined using the scale on the map. G. Where there is any uncertainty, contradiction, or conflict concerning the intended location of zoning district boundaries, the Zoning Board of Appeals shall interpret the exact location of zoning district boundaries. H. Insofar as some or all of the various districts may be indicated on the zoning map by patterns or colors that, for the sake of map clarity, do not cover public rights-of-way, it is intended that such district boundaries do extend to the center of the rights-of-way. Section 10.04 Zoning of Vacated Areas Whenever any street, alley, or other public way within the Township is vacated, such street, alley, or other public way shall automatically be classified in the same Zoning District as the property to which it attaches, and shall be subject to the standards for said Zoning District. Section 10.05 Zoning of Filled Land Whenever any fill is permitted in any stream or other body of water, the land created automatically and without further governmental action becomes subject to the same zoning regulations that are applicable to the land to which the newly-created land attaches. Section 10.06 District Requirements Buildings and uses in any district shall be subject to all applicable standards and requirements set forth in this Zoning Ordinance, including but not limited to Article 28.00, Schedule of Regulations. C1 Approve the Charter Township of York Special & Regular meeting minutes: August 11, 2026, as presented C2 Approve Disbursements: August 12, 2026 – September 8, 2026, as presented C3 Recognize reports from Clerk: Aug. 2026 Revenue/Expenditures C4 Recognize Treasurer’s Report, August 2026 C5 Recognize Board correspondence, August 2026 C6 Recognize written report from Building Official/Zoning Administrator, August 2026 C7 Recognize written report from Assessor, month of August 2026 C8 Recognize written report from Washtenaw County Sheriff’s Office (WCSO), month of July 2026 C9 Approve payment of $35,541.00 to Decker Agency for One-Year Public Policy Insurance Package C 10 Approve payment of $1,569 to Southeast Michigan Council of Governments for 2026 Annual Membership Dues C 11 Approve building permit refund request of $570.00 to Ekstrom Contracting LLC C 12 Approve payment of $1,450.00 to Bredell & Bredell for Facilitation of Steele v Charter Township of York, et al Case No. 25-002007-CH C 13 Recognize automatic renewal of York Township’s participation in the Washtenaw Urban County program for Fiscal Years 2027, 2028, and 2029 Moved by Zupi to approve the September 8, 2026, Consent Agenda as submitted. Seconded by McGovern. Discussion: None. Voice Vote: Aye: 7; Nay: 0; Absent: 0. Motion carried. REGULAR AGENDA Discussion: changes or corrections to the Regular Agenda. Moved by Zupi to approve the September 8, 2026, Regular Agenda as amended, adding New Business Item #7, Appointment to Non-Motorized Transportation Committee. Seconded by Hargrove. Discussion: None. Voice Vote: Aye: 7; Nay: 0; Absent: 0. Motion carried. VERBAL REPORTS Mike Siefker, Zoning/Building Depts. – August 2026 Building and Zoning reports given. BOARD REPORTS Trustee Hargrove – Saline Area Fire Department/Authority Fire Board met to approve the restated and rewritten cost recovery ordinance to reflect ‘authority’ instead of ‘department.’ The Chief is on a 6-month contract, and a 3% salary increase was approved retroactive to June 2026. Milan Area Fire Department Fire Board meets later this month. Trustee Neill – The Election Commission met 8/20/26 to establish the Absent Voter Count Board and appoint Election Inspectors. The City of Saline is honoring Saline Police Chief Marlene Radzik, who used to be a Sheriff’s Deputy assigned to York Township. Treasurer Louis – Taxes are due 9/14/26. Met with Township Insurer, Decker Insurance, to discuss the upcoming policy year’s coverage and rates; it was determined that a cyber policy should be added to properly cover the Township. More information regarding the cyber policy will come at the October Board meeting, as well as updates on digital communication efforts. Trustee McGovern – The Personnel Committee met this morning to discuss the digital communication coordinator job description and policy. The Committee also discussed the job description and pay rate for a Recording Secretary. The Committee will meet again in October. Trustee Gary – The Planning Commission has not met this month; it was scheduled to meet 9/14/26, but due to several absences, the meeting has been rescheduled to 9/21/26. Clerk Zupi – Ballots for the November General Election should be mailed in about 2 weeks. The Environmental Committee met 8/12/26 and discussed the Bulk Waste Event scheduled for 9/26/26, 9 a.m.–1 p.m. The Committee will meet tomorrow evening to continue planning logistics for the event. Supervisor Ludwig – Spoke with Washtenaw County Road Commission (WCRC) about a ‘reduced speed ahead’ sign near Willis Rd/High Creek Ct and the no-thru truck route on Willis Rd east of Carpenter Rd not appearing as such on WCRC’s website. WCRC tested a new brine solution on Arkona Rd for dust control. Roadwork on Sanford Rd should begin soon, beginning with culvert work. Milling and limestone should be started around 9/28/26. UNFINISHED BUSINESS: None NEW BUSINESS: 1. Non-Motorized Pathway Discussion Non-Motorized Committee Chair Bill Cook presented an update on Phase 1 (City of Saline to Whispering Pines Dr) of the pathway. Updates included design updates, grant and funding sources, and communication with residents. Phase 1 will be largely curb-and-gutter with a retaining wall. 2. Resolution #2026-20, Resolution of Support for the Willis Road Non-Motorized Pathway Project Moved by Zupi, seconded by Hargrove, to adopt Resolution #2026-20, Resolution of Support for the Willis Road NonMotorized Pathway Project. Discussion: Township Attorney Sarah Osburn present. Trustees raised concerns as to the language of the resolution regarding matching funds. Roll Call Vote: Aye: Hargrove, Neill, Louis, Ludwig, Zupi, Gary, McGovern Nay: None Abstain: None Absent: None Aye: 7; Nay: 0; Abstain: 0; Absent: 0. Motion carried. 3. Settlement Agreement Regarding 8501 Moon Road Moved by Zupi, seconded by Neill, to go into closed session under MCL 15.268(1)(e) to consult with the Township attorney regarding trial or settlement strategy in connection with Steele v York Township, Case No. 25-002007-CH currently pending in the Washtenaw County Circuit Court and York Township v Steele, Case No. 25YZ-2513 and 2514-ON currently pending in District Court at 7:45 p.m. Discussion: Building and Zoning Official Siefker and Planning Commissioner MacArthur invited to stay for closed session given their roles in the Township. Roll Call Vote: Aye: McGovern, Gary, Zupi, Ludwig, Louis, Neill, Hargrove Nay: None Abstain: None Absent: None Aye: 7; Nay: 0; Abstain: 0; Absent: 0. Motion carried. Moved by Louis, seconded by Hargrove, to terminate the closed session and re-open the regular session of the Board meeting at 8:17 p.m. Moved by Zupi, seconded by Gary, to approve the settlement agreement for District Case No. 25YZ-2513 and 2514-ON and Circuit Court Case No. 25-002007-CH, regarding the fence at 8501 Moon Rd, upon presentation of a signed settlement agreement with the following revision: operating sections of the gate, meaning the gate doors, are physically removed prior to lis pendes being released and District Court Cases being dismissed; and authorize Supervisor to sign. Discussion: None. Voice Vote: Aye: 7; Nay: 0; Absent: 0. Motion carried. 4. Survey of Mary McCann Park Moved by Louis, seconded by Gary, to approve the proposal from Nowak & Fraus Engineers (NFE) to survey the entirety of Mary McCann Park, not to exceed $5,500. Discussion: Possibility for NFE to use the Township side-by-side to traverse the park as traditional motor vehicles are not able to do so. Voice Vote: Aye: 7; Nay: 0; Absent: 0. Motion carried. 5. Saline Fire Authority Budget Discussion The Board discussed the Saline Area Fire Authority (SAFA) millage proposal on the November 3, 2026, ballot. If the proposal passes, the Township may reduce its existing Public Safety millage to avoid overlapping taxation for fire services. The current Public Safety millage expires at the end of 2028. The Board reviewed potential millage reductions and General Fund contributions. SAFA is preparing two preliminary 2027 budgets based on whether the millage passes. Supervisor Ludwig advised that the budgets are expected to be available for the Board’s consideration at the October meeting. The Board noted the limited timeframe following the November election to make any necessary millage and tax system adjustments before Winter 2026 tax bills are issued. The Board also discussed the Township’s continued MAFD commitment through June 2027 and the possibility of SAFA reimbursing or assuming the remaining commitment if its millage passes. The Board noted that WCSO changed to “true billing” for Police Service Units in June 2026, based on hours worked. This change, along with the Township’s historical $300,000–$600,000 annual contributions to the Public Safety Fund, will be considered when determining any adjustment to the Public Safety millage. 6. Comcast Business Fiber-Optic Internet Moved by Zupi, seconded by McGovern, to approve the services sales order agreement for fiber-optic internet with Comcast Business, as presented, and authorize Supervisor to sign. Discussion: Fiber-optic internet provides more reliability than what is currently being used. Voice Vote: Aye: 7; Nay: 0; Absent: 0. Motion carried. 7. Appointment to Non-Motorized Transportation Committee Moved by McGovern, seconded by Zupi, to appoint resident Beau LeFleur to the Non-Motorized Transportation Committee. Discussion: A quorum for the Committee has been difficult to establish due to work commitments and health concerns. Voice Vote: Aye: 7; Nay: 0; Absent: 0. Motion carried. PUBLIC COMMENT (five minutes maximum): None. ADJOURN: Moved by Gary, seconded by Zupi, to adjourn the Regular Board meeting at 8:51 p.m. Discussion: None. Voice Vote: Aye: 7; Nay: 0; Absent: 0. Motion carried. *** Newspaper of record: The Sun Times Website: www.twp-york.org CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF YORK WASHTENAW COUNTY, MICHIGAN RESOLUTION #2026 - 20 RESOLUTION OF SUPPORT FOR THE WILLIS ROAD NON-MOTORIZED PATHWAY PROJECT At a Regular Meeting of the Township Board of the Charter Township of York, Washtenaw County, Michigan held at the Township Hall in said Township, on the 8th day of September, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. PRESENT: Dave Ludwig, Sally Louis, Kayleigh Zupi, John Hargrove, Helen Neill, Jason McGovern, and Tom Gary ABSENT: None The following preamble and resolution were offered by Zupi and supported by Hargrove. WHEREAS, the Charter Township of York supports the construction of the Willis Road Non-Motorized Pathway Project (“Project”); and WHEREAS, a feasibility study of the Project was completed in 2019; and WHEREAS, the Charter Township of York Non-Motorized Transportation Committee (“Committee”) was established in 2022 and has facilitated public outreach including open houses held on Thursday, January 11, 2024, Thursday, January 9, 2025, and Wednesday, May 20, 2026, at the York Township Hall to provide an opportunity for all residents to express opinions, ask questions and discuss all aspects of the proposed Project; and WHEREAS, preliminary engineering for Phase I of the Project was completed in 2023; and WHEREAS, the Charter Township of York recognizes that in order to proceed with the Project, it will be necessary for the Township to obtain funding from outside sources in order to complete the project; and WHEREAS, the Committee has identified potential funding sources including but not limited to Michigan Department of Transportation/SEMCOG TAP; and WHEREAS, the Committee recommends that the Charter Township of York adopt this resolution of support for the Project and further to support and authorize the submission of applications for funding through the Michigan Department of Transportation/SEMCOG TAP in the amount of $2,078,652; and WHEREAS, the Charter Township of York recognizes that in order to receive funding, the Charter Township of York is obligated to (1) provide matching funds, (2) authorize a specific employee, official or agent to act as the Township representative during project development and to sign a project agreement upon receipt of a grant funding award, (3) commit to owning/operating the constructed facility and funding/implementing a maintenance plan/program in perpetuity or causing operations and maintenance to occur, and (4) commit to being responsible for engineering, permits, administration, potential cost overruns and any non-participating items including easement acquisition. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Charter Township of York Board of Trustees supports submitting an application for Michigan Department of Transportation/SEMCOG TAP for $2,078,652. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Charter Township of York is hereby making a financial commitment to the project in the amount of $200,000 in matching funds and $400,000 from other sources; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Washtenaw County Road Commission will act as the Charter Township of York’s Act 51 agency and project sponsor during project development and is authorized to sign a project agreement on behalf of the Charter Township of York upon receipt of a funding award; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Charter Township of York shall be responsible for engineering, permits, administration, potential cost overruns and any non-participating items including easement acquisition; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Charter Township of York will own, operate, and implement a maintenance plan, with dedicated funding, or will otherwise cause operations and maintenance to occur, in perpetuity for the facility constructed with TAP funds. 2 Roll Call Vote: Ayes: Hargrove, Neill, Louis, Ludwig, Zupi, Gary, McGovern Nays: None Absent: None Abstain: None RESOLUTION DECLARED ADOPTED. ___ Kayleigh Zupi, Clerk Charter Township of York Dated: September 8, 2026 CERTIFICATE I, Kayleigh Zupi, certify that the foregoing is a true and complete copy of Resolution #2026-20 adopted by the Township Board for Charter Township of York, County of Washtenaw, State of Michigan, at the Regular Meeting held on September 8, 2026, and that public notice of said meeting was given pursuant to Act No. 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, as amended. Stumbo Township Clerk Debbie Swanson Township Treasurer Stan Eldridge MEMORANDUM To: Ypsilanti Township Planning Commission From: Mark Yandrick, AICP, Planning Director cc: Brenda Stumbo, Ypsilanti Township Supervisor Doug Winters, McLain and Winters Sally Elmiger, Carlisle Wortman & Associates Date: October 22, 2026 Re: 1410 South Huron St., Special Land Use/Preliminary Site Plan for True Credit Union Background & Proposal The applicant, Heather Colonius on behalf of True Community Credit Union, is proposing to relocate from their existing facility at 1861 Whittaker Rd. to 1410 S. Huron St, which is adjacent to the new Culver’s Restaurant that is under construction. See the attached Carlisle Wortman reports which provides multiple options for Planning Commission to consider for review and consideration for approvals. Staff highlights the recommendation conditional of approval regarding the CMU block as Planning Commission needs to specifically approve it. However, staff notes that while adjacent properties use CMU block, there is color, contrast that make it look like brick and similar material appropriate for the Town Center Zoning District, which is from the Form Based Code. Conclusion/Recommendation Based on the Carlisle Wortman report, staff makes the following recommendations. Staff recommends APPROVAL of the Special Land Use for a drive through of a financial institution with the following one (1) condition: 1. The property owner must seek Site Plan Approval associated with this Special Land Use. Staff recommends APPROVAL of the Preliminary Site Plan with the following four (4) conditions: 1) Planning Commission only approves CMU block on the façade if the applicant adds more architectural compatibility, such as color, pattern, and contrast, with the adjacent commercial buildings to emulate something that appears more like brick or stone material to align with the Town Center design standards. 2) The applicant shall provide a signed written Easement Agreement for the adjacent Joe Township Supervisor Brenda L. Stumbo Township Clerk Debbie Swanson Township Treasurer Stan Eldridge Trustees John Newman II Gloria Peterson Karen Lovejoy Roe LaResha Thornton Hall parcel that reflects the preliminary agreement in the Letter of Intent. 3) The applicant shall provide a cross-access and maintenance Easement Agreement with Culver’s and Aldis regarding internal driveway. 4) The applicant shall address the following issues at the Final Site Plan stage: a. Modify Tree Protection Fencing detail on plans to indicate fencing is installed at or further away from the dripline of the trees to be protected. b. Adjust location of parking lot so that it is at least 10-feet from the south property line or seek a variance. c. Defer evaluation of Turning Map information to Fire Marshall. d. Add quantities of each proposed plant species to the Landscape Plant List table on Sheet C6.0. e. Revise parking lot layout and building location on Sheets E010 and E011 to illustrate the most up-to-date site design. Date: October 6, 2026 Preliminary Site Plan and Special Use Review For Ypsilanti Township, Michigan Applicant: True Community Credit Union (Represented by Heather Colonius) Project Name: True Community Credit Union Development and Drive-Through Plan Date: April 13, 2026 Latest Revision: August 25, 2026 Location: 1410 S. Huron St. (On west side of S. Huron Street, just north of Culver’s site) Note: The address of this site is 1410 S. Huron St. (per MapWashtenaw) Zoning: FB, Form Based District – Town Center; Site Type D Action Requested: Preliminary Site Plan and Special Use Approval PROJECT AND SITE DESCRIPTION The applicant is proposing to build a 3,000 square-foot credit union office with drive-through facilities on the west side of S. Huron St., just north of the new Culver’s restaurant and south of Joe Hall Drive. The site design includes three (3) drive-through lanes at the rear of the building. The project will also provide a vehicular connection between Joe Hall Drive, this site, and the Culvers and Aldi to the south. Other site features include parking, a pedestrian connection with the public sidewalk along S. Huron St., landscaping, and lighting. The subject site is zoned FB, Form Based Mixed Use – Town Center, and is categorized as a Site Type D. The 2.0-acre property was formed by splitting off 1.74-acres of land from the Culver’s site and combining it with 0.26-acres of property to the west that was owned by Ypsilanti Township. Financial institutions are permitted on a Site Type D and uses with drive-through facilities are allowed via special use. Singletenant, single-story buildings (Building Type B) are permitted. An aerial of the subject site is provided on the next page. Benjamin R. Carlisle, President John L. Enos, Vice President Paul Montagno, Principal Megan Masson-Minock, Principal Laura Kreps, Principal Brent Strong, Principal David Scurto, Principal Sally M. Elmiger, Principal Craig Strong, Principal Douglas J. Lewan, Principal Richard K. Carlisle, Past President/Senior Principal R. Donald Wortman, Past Principal True Community Credit Union & Drive-Through October 6, 2026 Figure 1. MASTER PLAN The site is designated as Township Core in the Master Plan and is intended to be the urbanized core of the community. The Township Core Special Area Plan (Page 72) states that this area will serve as the central gathering place and commercial base of the township. Buildout will be market responsive with a variety of uses including civic, regional and local commercial, hotels and restaurants, office, multiplefamily housing, and open space that will meet the daily needs of Township residents. A financial institution is consistent with the vision in the Master Plan for the Township Core. Applicable design concepts in the Master Plan (Page 58) that apply to this project include: • Architectural design must create an interesting visual experience for both sidewalk users at close range and for those viewing the skyline from a distance. • Design creativity with regard to materials will be encouraged, although low-quality materials or building designs that inhibit activity on the corridor will not be permitted. The building architecture, described on elevations on Sheet A200, uses pre-finished aluminum fascia, metal wall panels, masonry block, and limestone windowsills on the windows in the masonry block facades. The masonry blocks (concrete masonry units) are large format 12” x 24” blocks. The main block is “burnished” with an accent band being “split faced.” We question whether concrete masonry units/blocks meet the ordinance standard of a high-quality material. The design appears to be a corporate design for business identification. We suggest that the applicant could bring samples of the block to a meeting to better illustrate these materials. The Planning Commission should discuss the architectural design and its appropriateness for the Township Core envisioned in the Master Plan. Since the True Community Credit Union building will be directly next to Culver’s restaurant, we have provided both the proposed True Community Credit Union front façade and Culver’s front façade below: Figures 2 and 3. Culver’s Façade (Left) and Proposed True Community Credit Union Façade (Right) Items to be Addressed: 1) Planning Commission to discuss the architectural design, use of concrete masonry units on much of the building facades, and this material’s appropriateness as a “high-quality material” for the Township Core envisioned in the Master Plan. 2) Applicant could bring block samples to a Planning Commission meeting to better illustrate the proposed material. 3 True Community Credit Union & Drive-Through October 6, 2026 NATURAL FEATURES Topography: The subject site slopes down from S. Huron St., becomes somewhat flat, and then slopes down again to the storm drainage easement on the west side of the site. The west boundary of the site is approximately 14 feet lower than the elevation of the Huron St. sidewalk. Aldis and Culver’s raised the level of their sites to bring the finished floor of their building up to or slightly below the elevation of the Huron St. sidewalk adjacent to their property. The True Community Credit Union is doing the same. Their finished floor elevation is proposed as the same elevation as the Culver’s project. This consistency across multiple properties will create a pleasant, pedestrianforward pattern along S. Huron, helping to create the goals of the Township Core Special Area Plan. Woodlands/ Wetlands: The site currently has trees along S. Huron St., and to the north. Trees also exist on the neighboring property to the north that are proposed for removal to accommodate construction of a stormwater basin for this project. As requested, the tree tags numbered in the 1500’s are now listed on the Site Demolition / Tree Removal Plan (Sheet C1.1). In our previous review, we identified three (3) large trees that could be retained. These trees are: Tag No. 1549: 26.2” Cottonwood Tag No. 1550: 30” Cottonwood Tag No. 1551: 17” Cottonwood The revised Site Plan shows these trees will be retained, helping to maintain an appropriate scale of vegetation along the corridor as well as some of the existing character of the roadway. The project is proposing to remove 19 trees on the subject site, and an additional 19 trees on the neighboring property to the north. Sec. 24-67 of the Woodlands Protection ordinance does not require mitigation for tree removal that is conducted within the limits of construction. This submission includes a signed Letter of Intent with the property owner to the north, agreeing to allow True Community Credit Union to remove trees and construct and maintain a stormwater basin on the neighbor’s property. We would recommend that Preliminary Site Plan approval, if granted, be conditioned on the applicant providing a written signed Easement Agreement that reflects the preliminary agreement in the Letter of Intent. As requested, a Tree Protection Fence symbol is shown at the dripline of vegetation/trees to remain on the Site Plan and Grading Plan. Also, a Tree Protection Fence detail is provided. However, this detail should be amended to 4 True Community Credit Union & Drive-Through October 6, 2026 indicate that the fencing is located at or further away from the dripline of the tree to be protected. This can be done at the Final Site Plan review stage. The Site Plan and Grading Plan also has a note stating the following: “No vehicle, other construction equipment, or construction materials or debris shall be parked or stored within the dripline of any tree or plant material intended to be saved.” The pond to the west of this site is a constructed stormwater basin that serves the parcels along Joe Hall Drive. No impacts to this pond are proposed with this project. Items to be Addressed: 1) Recommend that Preliminary Site Plan approval, if granted, be conditioned on the applicant providing a signed written Easement Agreement that reflects the preliminary agreement in the Letter of Intent. 2) Modify Tree Protection Fencing detail on plans to indicate fencing is installed at or further away from the dripline of the trees to be protected at Final Site Plan stage. Mr. Abraham expressed concern for the future of the established community and urged the Planning Commission to “do the right thing” by considering the long-standing homes in the area. Sharon Conley – 1637 Wildcat Rd Sharon Conley stated that the Commission has a responsibility to consider the information submitted by residents. Ms. Conley outlined several possible land uses depending on the final zoning classification and urged the Commission to deny the rezoning request. OLD BUSINESS (PC-10-26) (OR206-26) Map Amendment (Rezoning) (PC-10-26) (OR-206-26) Map Amendment (Rezoning) Lynn Wilson Presented a petition to amend the zoning map that has been submitted by Nathan Waggner. The applicant is requesting approval to rezone 47.24 acres from Single Family Residential (R-1) to Multiple Family Residential (MF). The subject property is located at S. Scott Rd and Wildcat Rd., Section 15 of Bingham Township (Parcel ID: 030-015-200-010-50). Page | 4 Miles Roblyer addressed questions about the rezoning process, noting that planning and zoning procedures are highly specialized and often unfamiliar to residents until a project gains attention. He explained that the process is governed by the Michigan Zoning Enabling Act, and that a rezoning must occur before any site plan can be considered. He acknowledged public frustration but clarified that the Commission is required to follow the state-mandated sequence, which is why the rezoning is being addressed at this stage. Todd Krajniare, representing the developer, provided an overview of the development history and efforts undertaken over several years to identify feasible housing options for the community. He explained challenges related to infrastructure, particularly water and sewer capacity, and noted that single-family housing is not economically viable given current construction costs and local income levels. He described outreach to multiple builders and developers and stated that multi-family development was the only option that met market demand and affordability needs. He outlined the developer’s background, experience in small communities, and commitment to market-rate housing without subsidies. He also detailed the site selection process and explained why alternative locations were not viable due to zoning, land availability, and infrastructure constraints. He concluded that the proposed site meets planning criteria and provides an appropriate transition between nearby commercial, industrial, and residential uses. Nathan Waggner introduced himself as the engineer of record and addressed several technical aspects of the proposal. He noted that letters from the Board of Public Works indicate adequate utility capacity for the project. He stated that multi-family development generates less traffic per unit than single-family housing and that preliminary estimates show approximately one additional vehicle per minute during peak periods. He addressed drainage concerns, explaining that multi-family development can reduce impervious surface areas compared to single-family layouts and that all stormwater would be managed on site. He referenced studies indicating that adjacent property values are not negatively impacted by apartment developments. He discussed potential setbacks and buffering options, noting these will be addressed in detail at the site plan stage. He concluded by responding to questions regarding site layout, market conditions, and local housing needs. The Commission reviewed the required findings of facts related to the rezoning petition. Staff clarified that no identifiable conditions have changed to justify the amendment other than the applicant’s request. It was also stated that no administrative error occurred in the original Page | 5 zoning ordinance. An example was provided from a previous case where a GIS parcel number error required correction through rezoning. Commissioners discussed precedent, noting concerns about consistency between rural and urban areas and the importance of relying on the currently adopted Future Land Use Map, while noting the importance of the upcoming Comprehensive Plan update. Staff confirmed that utility providers indicated adequate public services, with traffic impacts to be addressed during any future development review. Commissioners considered whether the rezoning would affect environmental conditions, including nearby regulated wetlands and soil limitations, but noted these issues would be evaluated more specifically at the site plan stage. Staff reiterated that the findings must focus on the rezoning itself and potential uses within the MF district, independent of any particular development proposal. The Commission also confirmed that the request aligns with the adopted Future Land Use Map. Potential environmental impacts such as wastewater, drainage, and soil characteristics were discussed, with recognition that detailed analysis would occur during site plan review. (PC-11-26) (PSLU260004) High Grade Materials 9266 Snows Lake Road Greenville, MI 48838 Janes and Linda Kurscz 1030 ½ Vogel Street Ludington, MI 49431 3133 E Colony Road North E Colony Rd, East of N Willians Rd 090-026-400-005-00, 090-025-300-005-00 Section 25 & 26, Greenbush Township 100 acres Zoning & Future Land Use Information Existing Zoning: MR Mineral Resource Extraction (MR) It is recognized that minerals exist throughout Clinton County that are valuable for use in the county, region and state. However, inherent to mining extraction activities, there are impacts which require regulation in view of the noise, dirt, dust and temporary and permanent changes to the topography and environment. It is the intent of the County to regulate, inspect and monitor mining operations in order to minimize the existence of dangerously steep slopes, shifting earth, impairments or pollution of groundwater, surface water and the watershed, and to protect the air, water and natural resources and the public trust therein, and the health, safety and general welfare of the residents in the County through the following standards. The Clinton County Board of Commissioners Page 2 of 16 Future Land Use Map: recognizes that the exercise of zoning authority under MCL 125.3201(1) and (3) is an empowerment of the Board to plan and zone for a broad range of purposes. It defines the fundamental structure of a zoning ordinance by requiring a zoning plan to consider the interests of the entire community and to ensure that a broad range of land uses is permitted within that community. These provisions empower communities to plan for and regulate a broad array of land uses, taking into consideration the full range of planning concerns that affect the public health, safety, priorities and welfare of the community. Per the 2022 Clinton County Comprehensive Plan Update, the future land use designation is Agricultural Preservation (pp. 29). AGRICULTURAL PRESERVATION Areas designated on the Future Land Use Map as Agricultural Preservation (shown as the color green) are intended to identify areas of prime agricultural land used for production agriculture, small farms, low-density (large lot) residential, agricultural related businesses and industry in order to ensure the conservation of agricultural resource lands of long-term commercial significance for existing and future generations. Additionally, these lands should be protected from interference by adjacent uses which may affect the continued use of these lands for production of food and agricultural products. RURAL-TRANSITIONAL The Rural-Transitional land use designation (shown as the color white) describes various non-urban locations in the County where there is some existing low density residential development along County roadways and land is not suitable (due to topography, soils, vegetation, etc.) for agricultural purposes. The Rural Transitional land use designation provides a transition from prime agricultural land, identified as Agricultural Preservation, to Rural- Low Density Residential. Minimum lot size in the Rural-Transitional land use designation is five (5) acres. Farmland Agricultural Preservation 4.1. Site Plan Evaluation Layout 4.2. Project Narrative (MR) Mining/Extraction Operation Rural Transitional (A-2) (A-2) Farmland Farmland Rural Transitional Agricultural Preservation The proposed two parcel site is 100 acres in total (60 acres and 40 acres), with approximate dimensions of 996.14’W by 2637.74’D. The property is currently established farmland. The site in question contains larger sections of active farmland with tree screening between parcels, mostly near property lines. LEGISLATIVE BASIS FOR GCMPC REVIEW Part 361 of the Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act, 1994 Act 451 as amended, more commonly known as P.A. 116, enacted in 1974, establishes the right of a landowner, if all qualifications are met, to enter into a temporary restrictive agreement where the owner and the state agree to jointly hold the right to develop a parcel of farmland. This covenant is an agreement to not develop the property except as specifically stated within the agreement. The covenant runs with the land and is for a jointly agreed upon length of time (at least 10 years). Upon receipt of an application, the local governing body has 45 days to approve or reject the application. Within this 45-day period, the local governing body must seek comment from a number of bodies including “the county or regional planning commission”. Any comment received is strictly advisory as “these reviewing agencies do not have an approval or rejection power over the application”. II. STAFF ANALYSIS The request for comment from the Genesee County Metropolitan Planning Commission was received within the required 45-day period starting at the onset of application. The parcel located in Flushing Township, is identified as Section 19, T-8N, R-5E, Parcel #08-19-300-019. The parcel is 43 acres, of which 41 acres are used for cultivation. The parcel meets the criteria for eligibility as it is 40 acres and a minimum of 51% of the land is agriculturally active. The Flushing Township Zoning Map, updated in 2025, designates the parcel as Residential Suburban Agricultural (RSA). All neighboring parcels are identified as RSA as well.
